Exempted from the contribution of income from vacant Preacher's positions to the fund of the St. Petersburg Consistorial district are: <...> b) the Evangelical Lutheran Church of St. Peter and Paul [St. Peter] in St. Petersburg, which pays pensions to its own Preachers, as well as to their widows and orphans, according to special rules attached to this article (d).

2) Voluntary donations, which are permitted to be collected once a year at churches in favor of the Pastors' widows' and orphans' funds (e).

Note. In addition, the funds of the St. Petersburg and Moscow Consistorial districts have been granted the right to receive one percent above the general rate on their capital held in the Widows' Treasury of the St. Petersburg Board of Guardians (f).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 227, note 2. — (b) 1834 May 1 (7035). — (c) 1840 June 4 (13521). — (d) Ibid.; 1841 Nov. 18 (15036). — (e) 1834 May 1 (7035). — (f) 1841 Dec. 30 (15170); 1852 March 5, Imperial Directive.

V. On the jurisdiction over, and measures for the correction and punishment of, Preachers.

359. In matters relating to the clerical rank and to the duties of that rank, Preachers answer before the Consistories, according to the established order for this; in all other matters they are subject to the secular public offices, as appropriate.

• 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 225.

360. Preachers, for omissions and offenses in office or rank, are punished, depending on the seriousness of these offenses and the circumstances accompanying them, either 1) by reprimand, or 2) by removal from office, or finally 3) by deprivation of clerical rank.

*Ibid., § 228.*

361. A reprimand may be of two kinds: ordinary and severe.

*Ibid., § 229.*

362. An ordinary reprimand (einfacher Verweis) consists: 1) In a verbal or written remark from the appropriate Probst, Super-Intendent, or General Super-Intendent, in which the greater or lesser gravity of the Preacher's fault is pointed out to him, with an exhortation to be more careful in future. The Probst, Super-Intendent, or General Super-Intendent reports this to the Consistory. 2) In a written remark of the same kind from the Consistory. This reprimand may be accompanied by the imposition of a monetary fine, but not exceeding fifteen silver rubles.

*Ibid., § 230; 1839 Nov. 9 (12867).*

363. An ordinary reprimand from the Probst, Super-Intendent, or General Super-Intendent is given for minor offenses arising from thoughtlessness or negligence, which have given no occasion either for scandal or for complaint of infringement of anyone's rights. An ordinary reprimand from the Consistory is given for more serious offenses, as well as in cases where a Preacher is again found guilty of an omission for which he has already received a reprimand from his Probst, Super-Intendent, or General Super-Intendent.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 231.

364. A severe reprimand (scharfer Verweis) is given at a full session of the Consistory and is entered in the service record. This reprimand may, depending on the circumstances, be accompanied by a written announcement of the Preacher's fault to the clergy of the Probst district in which he is located, or even to the entire jurisdiction of the Consistory. — A severe reprimand may also, in some cases, be accompanied by the imposition of a monetary fine, not exceeding forty-five silver rubles (cf. Art. 362).

Note. If, owing to the remoteness of his residence, the Preacher cannot appear in person before the Consistory without significant difficulty, the reprimand is given to him in writing, and instead of summoning him to the Consistory it is ordered that this reprimand be announced to all Preachers of the Probst district in which the guilty party is located, or to the entire jurisdiction of the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 232; 1839 Nov. 9 (12867).*

365. A severe reprimand is imposed for a breach of duty (Disciplinar-Vergehen) confirmed by the offender's own admission or otherwise proven, especially for disobedience to the orders of the authorities and for offensive written or verbal remarks about such orders, as well as for other more serious offenses, provided it is reliably known that they were committed not out of malicious intent, but through carelessness or misunderstanding.

Note. When by a violation of the duties of subordination the higher spiritual or secular authority is insulted, the guilty party is subjected to the strictest punishment; but if, in showing disobedience to his superior, the Preacher has also dared to insult his honor, then for this he is subjected to a further special penalty on the basis of the general laws on this subject.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 233. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 327

366. Removal from office (remotio) is imposed for more serious offenses against one's office or rank, or for numerous offenses that have become publicly known at the same time. It is also imposed on Preachers found guilty anew of offenses for which they had already received a strict reprimand from the Consistory, as well as those who, by a sentence of the secular court that has entered into legal force, have been sentenced for a criminal offense to a punishment which, although it does not deprive them of honor, may nonetheless demean the clerical rank. Together with the removal of a Preacher from office, depending on the circumstances of the case, there may also be joined a prohibition against ever again appointing him to any Pastoral position, and a special announcement thereof to all Preachers subordinate to the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 234.*

367. Deprivation of clerical rank (Cassation) is imposed for the most serious offenses against one's office or rank, or when a Preacher is sentenced by the secular court for a criminal offense to deprivation of all rights of status, or to the loss of all special rights and privileges attached to him personally and by status, or of certain personal rights and privileges.

*Ibid., § 235; 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Arts. 19, 24, 46, 53.*

368. Preachers may not be deprived of clerical rank, nor removed from office, except by a formal judicial sentence, or by a special Supreme command.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 236.

369. A criminal case in which a Preacher has been sentenced by the secular court to one of the punishments specified in Article 367, after review by the higher local criminal court and examination by the Governor of the province, is submitted, before execution of the sentence, for review to the Governing Senate, and from the Governing Senate is presented for the Supreme consideration, and is not finalized without the confirmation of His Imperial Majesty.

1785 Apr. 21 (16187) Art. 13; 1799 Mar. 18 (18894); 1802 Sept. 8 (20405) Art. 20; 1806 Jan. 10 (21991); 1814 Aug. 29 (25668) Art. 4; 1820 Jul. 15 (28358); 1826 Sept. 24 (596) Art. 4; 1829 Oct. 26 (3261); 1846 Jan. 21 (19640); cf. Digest of Local Statutes of the Baltic (Ostsee) Governorates, part II, Arts. 924 and 925, per the Continuation.

370. Upon the Supreme confirmation of the sentence (Art. 369) and its return to the proper local court for execution, that court notifies the Consistory thereof, so that it may deprive the condemned Preacher of his clerical rank before the sentence is carried out in its other parts.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 238, item 1; cf. the enactments cited under Art. 369.

371. The decree on deprivation of clerical rank is carried into execution in one of two ways: either 1) by demanding from the condemned man his charter of clerical rank (Ordinations-Schein) and the insignia thereof, or 2) by the solemn removal of these insignia from him and the confiscation of the charter in a full session of the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 237; cf. the enactments cited under Art. 369.*

372. If, owing to the remoteness of the Consistory's residence, important delay might result from communicating with it under Article 370, then the provincial authority announces to the condemned man that, by force of the judicial sentence concerning him confirmed by the Supreme authority, he is deprived of his clerical rank, and communicates this to the proper Consistory for information.

*Ibid., § 238, item 2; cf. the enactments cited under Art. 369.*

373. A Preacher deprived of clerical rank under Articles 367-372, even if he should subsequently receive a pardon, remains forever deprived of that rank.

*Ibid., § 239; cf. the enactments cited under Arts. 367-372.*

374. In addition to the punishments established by the preceding articles, Preachers may, in certain cases specified below, be subjected to temporary removal from office (suspension). This, however, is not considered a punishment, but only a necessary precautionary measure.

*Ibid. § 240.*

375. A Preacher is temporarily removed from office: 1) when he is caught in the very commission of a criminal offense, or 2) when, on strong suspicion of such an offense, he is taken into custody by the secular court, or 3) when he falls under investigation for a grave offense against his office or rank entailing removal from office or even deprivation of clerical rank, or 4) when he is accused of committing such an offense and has confessed to it, or finally 5) when so strong a suspicion rests upon him that, during the course of the investigation, scandal to the parish might result from his continuing to perform the Preacher's duties.

*Ibid., § 241.*

376. Of any necessary arrest of a Preacher for a criminal offense, the secular authorities notify the Consistory, in advance where possible, or at least immediately after the arrest, so that the Consistory, having at the same time removed him from office, may take the necessary measures to entrust the performance of his duties to another and to dispatch one of its own members, or another clerical dignitary, to the investigation [(a)].

Note. The vote of the deputy in adjudicating a case in court is counted equally with the votes of the other members of the court (b).

(a) Ibid., § 242. — (b) Digest of Local Statutes of the Baltic (Ostsee) Governorates, part II, Art. 922.

377. A Preacher removed from office is obliged to give to whoever performs his duties during that time one half of everything received in that position, both the fixed maintenance and the special incomes (casuelle Einkünfte) for the performance of spiritual rites.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 243.

378. Of every Preacher temporarily removed from office, or entirely removed therefrom, as well as of the deprivation of his clerical rank, the Consistory immediately and in detail reports to the General Consistory, which presents this report to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

*Ibid., § 244.*

379. For disseminating a doctrine not in accord with Holy Scripture as explained in the Symbolic Books of the Evangelical Lutheran Church (Art. 134), and with the rules of that Church, a Preacher is punished either with an ordinary or a strict reprimand, or even with removal from office, DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 329

depending on the seriousness of the fault, that is, on the nature and tendency of the false opinions disseminated by him, and on whether he had in doing so any unlawful evil intent.

*Ibid., § 245.*

380. A Preacher who disseminates false opinions and doctrine not deliberately, but out of thoughtlessness or incomplete understanding of the force of the words of Holy Scripture or of the expressions used by himself, is to be first admonished and instructed by his immediate superiors; if these instructions and admonitions prove unsuccessful and he is again found guilty of the same carelessness, then, depending on the circumstances, he may be subjected to an ordinary or even a strict reprimand, and finally, in case of persistence, in accordance with the provisions of the preceding Article 379, to removal from office.

*Ibid., § 246.*

381. Deviation from the order of public worship and sacred rites established in the Church Agenda (Art. 140, note) is punished, depending on its seriousness, with an ordinary or strict reprimand, if indeed it is found by the immediate superiors of the Preacher and the local Consistory that it is not sufficient to confine matters to mere light remarks or admonitions through the Probst or Superintendent. But for repeated violation of the rules prescribed in the Liturgical Agenda, especially the most important ones, if the admonitions and other corrective measures employed prove unsuccessful, the guilty party may be sentenced to removal from office.

*Ibid., § 247.*

382. If the order of worship is violated by a Preacher, even without overt unlawful evil intent, to such a degree that strong scandal results among his parishioners to the detriment of piety and of the due reverence for the sacred rites, then he is immediately sentenced to removal from office, and, depending on the circumstances, even to deprivation of rank.

*Ibid., § 248.*

383. If a Preacher, out of negligence or laziness, avoids fulfilling the duty of visiting the sick in order to ease their sufferings through spiritual ministration, he is punished for this, first with an ordinary and then with a strict reprimand from the Consistory, and, should he fail to correct himself, with removal from office.

*Ibid., § 249.*

384. For the performance of invalid marriages the following punishments are imposed on a Preacher:

1) For performing a marriage which by law must be recognized as invalid, the Preacher, in the case where he has done so knowingly, is sentenced to deprivation of clerical rank and to imprisonment for a term of one to two years. When, however, he is found guilty only of an excusable error, arising more or less from a concurrence of particular circumstances, he is subjected: the first time to a strict reprimand, and the second time to removal from office (a).

2) For joining in marriage persons already bound by a marital union, in the case where this has been done by the Preacher through an excusable error, arising more or less from a concurrence of particular circumstances, he is subjected the first time to a strict reprimand, the second time to a monetary fine of from fifty to two hundred rubles, and the third time to deprivation of clerical rank. But if the Preacher is found to have known of the unlawfulness of the marriage he performed, then even the first time he is sentenced to deprivation of rank and to imprisonment for a term of six months to one year. And when it is proven that the Preacher also assisted the person bound by a prior marriage in deceiving the other person, who, unaware of this, entered into the unlawful marriage with him, then he is sentenced to the punishments established in the Code of Punishments, Article 133, for complicity in a crime (b).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 250; 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2067. — (b) 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2048.

385. If a Preacher, contrary to the rules established above in Chapter Four, performs, out of some mercenary or other personal motive, a marriage forbidden by the laws, even though not considered invalid, he is immediately removed from office and subjected to deprivation of clerical rank; when, on the contrary, he was merely led into an error excusable given the circumstances of the case, then the first time he receives only a strict reprimand; but in case of a further such carelessness, he, as unreliable, is removed from office with a prohibition against ever again appointing him to a position.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 251; 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2067.

386. To the punishments established in Article 384, item 1, and in Article 385, and on the same basis, is also subjected that Preacher who, although he did not himself perform the marriage forbidden by the laws, nevertheless by testimony, by an announcement in church, or by some other action pertaining to his office, gave another Preacher occasion to perform it.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 252; 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2067.

387. For performing a marriage without observing the rules prescribed above in Chapter Four regarding the announcement of banns and other precautionary measures, when there was no special permission for this, a Preacher is subjected, depending on the circumstances that more or less aggravate or diminish his fault, the first time to a reprimand, more or less strict, and the second time to removal from office, with a prohibition against ever again appointing him to a parish. He is subjected to the same punishments for marrying anyone who has arrived temporarily in his parish, without proper certification that this person is not already married.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 253; 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2069.

388. If a Preacher, without the authorization of the higher authority empowered to grant it, permits himself to declare any marriage dissolved, or to bless the separation, even if only temporary, of spouses from bed and board, then he is subjected for this either to a strict reprimand, or to removal from office, or to deprivation of rank, at the discretion of his ecclesiastical superiors.

1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 2070.

389. If an Evangelical Lutheran Preacher receives into his Church a member of the Orthodox Church, he is immediately removed from office and deprived of rank in the manner established above (Arts. 367-372).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 254. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 332

390. If a Preacher (Art. 389) knowingly admits Orthodox persons to confession or communion, or their children to baptism according to the rites of the Evangelical Lutheran Church, he is subjected for this, the first time to removal from his position for a term of six months to one year, and the second time to deprivation of clerical rank and being placed under police supervision. For performing any of these spiritual rites for Orthodox persons through ignorance, he is subjected to a strict reprimand, as for carelessness inconsistent with the importance of his rank (a). For performing a marriage between a person of the Orthodox and a person of the Protestant confession, before it has been performed by an Orthodox Priest, when there is no formal certification available from the proper ecclesiastical authority that, under the rules of the Orthodox Church, no obstacles exist to this marriage, the Preacher, depending on whether or not obstacles to that marriage subsequently appeared, and on other circumstances more or less aggravating or diminishing his fault, is subjected: either to a monetary fine of ten to fifty rubles, or to temporary removal from office for a term of two to six months, or to removal from his position (b).

(a) 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) Art. 201. — (b) Ibid., Art. 2068.

391. A Preacher who, without proper permission, receives into the Evangelical Lutheran Church a member of one of the other Christian Churches (besides the Orthodox Church, per Art. 389) that enjoy equal freedom of confession of their faith in Russia, is removed from office. — For performing spiritual rites for members of these Churches, without proper permission to do so, if this is done not by mistake but knowingly, especially when there is also revealed an intention to induce a change of faith, the Preacher is punished with removal from office.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 255.

<...>

393. If a Preacher leads a scandalous and depraved life, and repeated admonitions from his superiors and ordinary and strict reprimands from them and from the Consistory fail to produce in him the desired correction, then the local Consistory sentences him to removal from his position, or, depending on the seriousness of the accusation and the scandal, even to deprivation of clerical rank.

*Ibid., § 257.*

394. If a Preacher is accused of some violation of his official duties not specifically named in the preceding articles, then the Consistory, in examining this accusation, takes into consideration: 1) the greater or lesser importance of the duty he violated and the scandal, harm, or infringement of rights resulting therefrom; 2) his motives in committing the offense, whether from thoughtlessness or from unlawful evil intent; 3) the opinion of his parishioners about him and the degree of their attachment to him; and finally, 4) the reports about him from the Probst and the Superintendent, or the General Superintendent. On the basis of these considerations, the Consistory either instructs the Preacher's immediate superior to admonish and instruct him, or issues him, on its own part, a more or less strict reprimand, or finally, should all these corrective measures prove insufficient, sentences him to removal from his position, and, for very serious offenses harmful in their consequences to the whole parish or to the whole Evangelical Lutheran Church, even to deprivation of clerical rank.

*Ibid., § 258.*

Section Three.

On Sextons and Organists.

395. The sextons, cantors, organists, bell-ringers, and the like, attached to churches of the Protestant confession, although called church servants, serve by hire and are not counted among the clergy.

1850 Jan. 11 (23817) § 5, note 3; 1857 Jun. 3, Statute on the National Census, § 5, note 3.

396. For the position of sexton, literate people, knowledgeable in choral singing and having presented proper guarantees of their reliability, are chosen by the parish Preacher together with the Church Councils.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 259.

397. The sexton must assist the Preacher in everything pertaining to church service, and must show due obedience both to him and to the Church Council.

*Ibid., § 260.*

398. The Preacher, together with the Church Councils, may dismiss and remove a sexton from office. In case of disagreement between them regarding the choice, dismissal, or removal of a sexton, they seek the resolution of the Consistory (a).

Note. Those sextons of the Protestant confession who at the same time perform the duties of school teachers are exempted from conscription duty while holding these positions, though they are not exempted from paying the poll tax (b).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 261. — (b) 1839 Jun. 30 (12496).

399. Organists are appointed, dismissed, or removed in the same manner as sextons (Arts. 396 and 398).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 262.

400. Organists, in the performance of their office, are obliged to carry out exactly the instructions of the Preacher and of the Church Councils.

*Ibid., § 263.*

##### CHAPTER SIX.

On the Higher Clerical Dignitaries.

Section One.

On Probsts.

401. Probst districts in the Empire are formed, in consideration of local circumstances, from a greater or lesser number of Evangelical Lutheran parishes. In 1832 the following were designated: three in the Governorate of St. Petersburg, eight in Livland, eight in Estland, seven in Courland, DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 333

one in Vilna, two in the Saratov colonies, and two in the German colonies of the southern region.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 264.

402. Preachers of those Evangelical Lutheran parishes which, in 1832, were not attached to any Probst district, remain, until further arrangements, under the direct authority of the Consistories and the General Superintendents or Superintendents. If the establishment of a new Probstship, or any change in the extent of existing Probst districts, should prove necessary, the local Consistories report this to the General Consistory, which presents its opinion thereon to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, for report to His Imperial Majesty.

*Ibid., § 265.*

403. In the event of the death of a Probst, or of a grave illness preventing him from performing his office, his place is taken, until the appointment of a new Probst, by the senior in service in that district, or by another Preacher chosen by the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 266.*

404. When a vacancy arises for a Probst, the Consistory summons all the Preachers of that Probst district to elect two candidates for the vacant position, or requests their opinions in writing. The Consistory, through the General Consistory, presents these candidates, with its own conclusion, to the Ministry of Internal Affairs for the confirmation of one of them.

*Ibid., § 267.*

405. Probsts are subordinate directly to the General Superintendents and Consistories, and are themselves the immediate superiors of the Preachers belonging to their districts. They convey to them all the instructions of the ecclesiastical authorities, receive from them reports for presentation to the higher authorities, and, as their closest overseers and mentors, observe their teaching, moral life, and exactness in the performance of their duties. Probsts submit annually to the General Superintendents brief lists of themselves and of the Preachers subordinate to them, as well as conduct reports on the candidates for the clergy located in their district, according to the prescribed form.

*Ibid., § 268.*

406. If a Probst, without harmful loss of time to the matter, or for other reasons, cannot address his submission to the General Superintendent, he has the right to apply directly to the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 269.*

407. A Probst is obliged to conduct, at least once every three years, visitations of all the churches belonging to his district, having with him, if possible, Ecclesiastical assistants.

*Ibid., § 270, item 1.*

408. Visitations must be conducted, as far as possible, on Sundays, and each time, at least a week before the visitation, the Preacher must be notified thereof; he announces this to the parish from the pulpit. The Probst, for his part, also notifies the patrons and the Church Council of that parish of the intended visitation.

*Ibid., items 2 and 3.*

409. A visitation always begins with a solemn service. The sermon is delivered by the parish Preacher, on a text given by the Probst; then he explains a brief catechism to the assembled youth, in order to demonstrate his method of teaching it; after him the Probst himself examines the youth, and, if he considers it necessary, also other parishioners, in their knowledge of the Law of God. The Probst asks the Preacher whether he has anything to declare about the state of his parish in general. Thereupon the Preacher leaves the church, and the Probst puts the same question to the parishioners, records the answer, and dismisses them, having given them a suitable admonition on this occasion. He detains those who say that they have something in particular to declare to him. After this the Probst requires from the Preacher, the church servants, and the peasant church elders detailed and precise information as to how they perform their duties, in what relations they stand to one another and to the parish, and likewise concerning the religious and moral condition of the parishioners, the state of the schools and charitable institutions, the number and behavior of the clerical candidates present in that parish, the observance of Sundays and other solemn days, the order of divine service and the administration of the sacraments, burials, and generally everything pertaining to the church. He also requires information as to whether the payments due to the Preacher and church servants are being properly made; he then examines the church books, the church chronicle, the parish archive, and the church plate in the possession of the Preacher.

*Ibid., items 4 and 7.*

410. The Probst may, if he considers it necessary, require from the Preacher the drafts or outlines (Dispositionen) of his sermons as well.

*Ibid., item 8.*

411. The Probst is obliged, by means of advice and admonitions, to correct any omissions or disorders he finds during the visitation; of those which he cannot correct or stop in this manner, he reports to the Consistory.

*Ibid., item 9.*

412. The Probst must keep a record of everything that takes place at the visitation. This record is signed by him, by the Preacher, and, as witnesses, by some of those Church Wardens or other persons present at the visitation. The record remains in the church archive and serves as the basis for the next visitation; the Probst submits to the Consistory a copy thereof and the draft of the sermon delivered on this occasion by the parish Pastor.

*Ibid., item 10.*

413. In parishes not subordinate to Probsts, visitations are conducted by the General Superintendents or Superintendents; but in the case of very great distance from the residence of the General Superintendent or Superintendent, the Consistories entrust this to one of the Preachers.

Note 1. In those parishes where special rules for visitation had been established prior to 28 December 1832, the former order in this respect continues to be observed thereafter as well (a). DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 335

Note 2. During the visitation of their districts, Probsts receive relay conveyances (Vorspann) from the parishes. Each Probst in the colonies of the southern region is granted from the treasury, once every three years, a fixed monetary allowance for travel expenses during visitation journeys (b).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 270, note. — (b) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870), establishment tables, Art. VII, note; 1838 Jan. 18 (10899).

414. Probsts hold the title: Hochehrwürden; during divine service and on other solemn occasions they wear the official vestment established for Preachers (Art. 347).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 271.

415. Complaints of a Probst against Preachers, and of Preachers against a Probst, are submitted to the General Superintendent, as appropriate. He endeavors to settle their disputes amicably, and, failing success, submits the complaints for resolution to the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 272.*

416. If parishioners, a patron, or Church Wardens are dissatisfied with an order of the Probst, or believe that their rights with respect to church property are being violated, they turn with a complaint about this to the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 273.*

417. Probsts, like all other Evangelical Lutheran Preachers, use the seal of their church in official correspondence; their letters and packages sent under this seal are dispatched without payment of postage by weight.

*Ibid., § 274.*

Section Two.

On the General Superintendents, Superintendents,

and on the title of Evangelical Lutheran Bishops.

418. The higher ecclesiastical superiors of the Probsts in the Governorates of Livland, Estland, and Courland, and in the districts of the St. Petersburg and Moscow Consistories, are called General Superintendents, and the superiors of the Preachers on the island of Ösel and in the cities of Riga and Reval are called Superintendents.

Note. The General Superintendent of the Estland clergy is always also the Pastor of the Reval Cathedral church (Domkirche).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 275 and note.

419. For the positions of General Superintendent of Livland, Courland, and Estland, and of the Superintendent of Ösel, two candidates each are elected by the local nobility, and for the positions of Superintendent in Riga and Reval, likewise two candidates each, by the Magistrates of those cities. The elected candidates are presented, through the Governor-General of the Baltic Governorates and the Ministry of Internal Affairs, for the Supreme consideration of His Imperial Majesty. — The Ministry, in its report on these candidates, also presents the opinion of the General Consistory obtained regarding them. — For the positions of the St. Petersburg and Moscow General Superintendents, the General Consistory likewise presents to the Ministry of Internal Affairs two candidates each, for report to His Imperial Majesty.

*Ibid., § 276.*

420. The installation of General Superintendents and Superintendents into office is performed solemnly, by order of the General Consistory, in accordance with the order set forth in the Church Agenda.

*Ibid., § 277.*

421. General Superintendents and Superintendents, as the highest ecclesiastical superiors of the Probsts and other Evangelical Lutheran clergy belonging to their Consistorial districts, as well as of the clerical candidates, and as representatives of the Consistories, are obliged, in their personal dealings with subordinate clergy, to promote by all means at their disposal the exact fulfillment of the instructions of these bodies and their general duty of overseeing the proper course of all church affairs in the district. They must ensure that the teaching of the Preachers, in its spirit and in all particulars, accords with Holy Scripture and the explanations of the Symbolic Books, and that all clergy properly perform their duties, edifying their parishioners by the example of a moral life, ceaselessly perfecting themselves in the sciences necessary to their rank, and, in performing spiritual rites and sacred ceremonies, not departing arbitrarily from the rules of the Church Agenda. They must endeavor, without delay, to eliminate, stop, or prevent and correct anything in the official conduct and manner of life of the clergy subordinate to them that is contrary to this Church Statute or to the provisions of the Agenda; but they are obliged to notify the Consistory both of this, and of those cases in which they are unable by their own authority to stop some disorder, as well as, generally, of all their observations of importance for any reason with respect to the district entrusted to them.

*Ibid., § 278.*

422. General Superintendents and Superintendents ordinarily direct the candidate examinations and spiritual conferences (colloquium). They also, upon the transfer of Preachers, satisfy themselves by means of spiritual conferences as to their merit and knowledge.

*Ibid., § 279.*

423. General Superintendents and Superintendents, on the basis of the rules of the Church Liturgical Agenda, ordain, and, when local circumstances permit, also install into office the Preachers of their Consistorial district. By them also, and likewise on the basis of the rules of the Liturgical Agenda, the consecration of churches is performed, and only in case of great distance, or of illness of the General Superintendent or Superintendent, may the Consistory entrust a Probst or other ecclesiastical person to install a Preacher into office, or to consecrate a church.

*Ibid. § 280.*

424. General Superintendents and Superintendents present to the Consistory annually brief service records of the Probsts and Preachers and conduct reports on the clerical candidates located in their district, with an indication of their own opinion of them, according to the established form (a).

Note. In the column concerning the abilities of clergy to perform their duties, General Superintendents and Superintendents make their notations without any participation whatsoever of the secular authority (b).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 281; 1852 Jan. 28 (25944) Art. 143, item 4. — (b) 1834 Jul. 19 (7287). DOCUMENTS___________________________________________________________________________ 337

425. General Superintendents and Superintendents are obliged, at least once every six years, to conduct a visitation of all the Probst districts, and, where there are no Probstships, of all the parishes of their district. In these visitations they follow the same rules as are prescribed for Probst visitations, and pay particular attention to the conduct of the Probsts and their relations with the Preachers of their districts. They are also obliged to examine with due diligence the Probst church archives, and, moreover, have the right, should they consider it necessary, to be present also at the Probst visitations (a).

Note. Regarding the allocation of funds to General Superintendents and Superintendents for visitation travel, the Consistories of St. Petersburg, Moscow, Livland, Estland, and Courland request special authorization each time (b).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 282. — (b) Ibid., establishment tables I, II, III, IV, V, note.

426. Besides these regular visitations, they may from time to time undertake an unexpected visitation of some parish, either by order of the Consistory or at their own discretion, having, however, first notified the Consistory thereof.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 283.

427. In those parishes in which General Superintendents or Superintendents themselves hold the position of Preacher, visitations are likewise conducted at least once every six years. This is entrusted to a special Commission appointed by the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 284.*

428. General Superintendents and Superintendents, during divine service and on other solemn occasions, wear the vestment established for all Evangelical Lutheran Preachers, and, in addition, on their breast, as a mark of distinction granted to them by His Imperial Majesty, a smooth gold cross on a gold chain, which is placed upon them by the President of the Consistory upon their installation into office.

*Ibid., § 285.*

429. General Superintendents and Superintendents hold the title Hochwürden.

*Ibid., § 286.*

430. In correspondence relating to the affairs of their office, General Superintendents and Superintendents use a special seal bearing the image of a cross and the inscription: Siegel des N. General-Superintendenten, or: des N. Superintendenten. Their letters and packets sent under this seal are dispatched without payment of postage fees.

*Ibid., § 287.*

431. Clergy who, as a mark of special Imperial favor and in reward for many years of distinguished service, are elevated to the honorary rank of Evangelical Lutheran Bishops, likewise bear the title Hochwürden, the same official vestments and insignia, and in their dealings with the Consistory and the subordinate clergy are governed by the same rules that define the rights and duties of General Superintendents and Superintendents.

*Ibid., § 288.*

432. All senior clergy dignitaries of the Evangelical Lutheran confession, as well as their Preachers and Adjuncts upon entering office, and candidates of the clergy upon receiving the right to preach (venia concionandi), take an oath of allegiance in the service of His Imperial Majesty in the established manner, on the general basis.

*Ibid., § 289.*

##### CHAPTER SEVEN.

On Consistories.

Section One.

On the local Consistories.

433. All Evangelical Lutheran parishes in the Empire, with the exception of those located in the Transcaucasian colonies of foreign settlers, are under the jurisdiction of the following local Consistories: 1) St. Petersburg, 2) Livonia, 3) Estonia, 4) Courland, 5) Moscow, 6) Ösel, 7) Riga, and 8) Reval.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 290; 1847 Jul. 29 (21450).

434. The districts of these Consistories comprise:

1) In the district of the St. Petersburg Consistory: the Evangelical Lutheran parishes of the governorates of St. Petersburg, with the cities of Kronstadt and Narva, Novgorod, Pskov, Vologda, Olonets, Arkhangelsk, Kostroma, Yaroslavl, Smolensk, Chernigov, Volhynia, Podolia, Kiev, Poltava, Yekaterinoslav, Taurida, Kherson with the city of Odessa, the Bessarabia region, and the Russian-American colonies.

2) In the district of the Livonia Consistory: the Evangelical Lutheran parishes of Livonia governorate, except those located on the islands of Arensburg uyezd and those belonging to the jurisdiction of the city of Riga. In this latter city, however, the parish of St. James belongs to the jurisdiction of the Livonia Consistory.

3) In the district of the Estonia Consistory: the Evangelical Lutheran parishes of Estonia governorate, except the churches and parishes located within the city of Reval itself; of these, only the parish of the Domkirche (Toompea Church) belongs to the jurisdiction of the Estonia Consistory (a).

Note. Also under the jurisdiction of the Estonia Consistory, under the supervision of the Ministry of Public Education, is the Toompea Orphan School existing in Reval. To reduce correspondence, the Consistory, in matters concerning the appointment and promotion in rank of teachers and in other matters personally relating to their service, applies through the Curator of the Dorpat educational district to the Ministry of Public Education, which is authorized to submit representations thereon for further consideration wherever appropriate (b).

4) In the district of the Courland Consistory: the Evangelical Lutheran parishes of the governorates of Courland, Vitebsk, Mogilev, Minsk, Vilna, Grodno, and Kovno (c).

5) Around the Moscow Consistory: the Evangelical Lutheran parishes of the governorates of Moscow, Tver, Kaluga, Tula, Ryazan, Vladimir, Nizhny Novgorod, Penza, Tambov, Voronezh, Kursk, Oryol, Kharkov, Saratov, Simbirsk, Kazan, Vyat-

DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 339

ka, Perm, Samara, Orenburg, Astrakhan, and Stavropol, the Siberian and Transcaucasian territories.

6) In the district of the Ösel Consistory: the Evangelical Lutheran parishes of the islands of Ösel, Moon, Runö, and other small islands belonging to Arensburg uyezd.

7) Around the Riga City Consistory: the Evangelical Lutheran parishes of the city of Riga and the Riga church district (Stadt und Patrimonialgebiet), with all the Evangelical Lutheran churches located therein, with the sole exception of the church of St. James and its parish (item 2).

8) In the district of the Reval City Consistory: the Evangelical Lutheran parishes of all churches located in this city, except only the Domkirche (item 3), and in addition the rural communities belonging to the Estonian city church (d).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 291, item 1: 1839 Jun. 13 (12434); 1847 Jul. 29 (21450). - (b) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 291, items 2, 3; 1843 May 9 (16602); 1847 Jul. 29 (21450). - (c) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 291, item 4; 1842 Dec. 18 (16347); 1847 Jul. 29 (21450). - (d) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 291, items 5-8; 1847 Jul. 29 (21450); 1848 Jan. 27 (21943).

435. The Evangelical Lutheran Consistories are composed of a secular President, a clerical Vice-President — whose place is always occupied by the General Superintendent or Superintendent of that Consistorial district — and an equal number of secular and clerical Assessors. All members must belong to the Evangelical Lutheran confession. In the Consistories of St. Petersburg, Livonia, Estonia, Courland, and Riga, there shall be two secular and two clerical Assessors each, while in Moscow, Ösel, and Reval there shall be one of each, secular and clerical.

Note 1. The clerical Vice-President, in the absence of the President, performs his duties in the Consistory; in the absence of both, the senior secular Assessor presides (a).

Note 2. The Chairmen and members of the Evangelical Lutheran Consistories, as well as the officials of the Chancelleries of these Consistories, may hold other positions, retaining the salary attached thereto, provided that the duties combined with them do not interfere with their work in the Consistory (b).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 292. - (b) 1833 Nov. 4 (6547).

436. The Presidents of the Consistories of St. Petersburg and Moscow are appointed by His Imperial Majesty upon the representation of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, which requests beforehand the opinion of the General Consistory concerning the proposed candidates. To fill vacancies of Presidents in the Consistories of Livonia, Estonia, Courland, and Ösel, two candidates each are elected, by order of the Baltic Governor-General, by the local nobility, and in the City Consistories of Riga and Reval by the City Magistrates — in Livonia and Estonia governorates and on the island of Ösel from among the members of the Landrat Colleges, in Courland governorate from among the members of the Courland Oberhofgericht, and in Riga and Reval from among the learned Burgomasters. Upon the election of candidates, the nobility or Magistrate reports thereon to the Governor-General, who communicates this election to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, stating his opinion of the candidates. The Ministry of Internal Affairs submits them for the Highest consideration.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 293; 1848 [1847] Jul. 29 (21450).

437. To fill vacancies of secular and clerical Assessors in the Consistories of St. Petersburg and Moscow, these Consistories submit, through the General Consistory, two candidates for each place to the Ministry of Internal Affairs. For secular Assessors of the Livonia, Estonia, Courland, and Ösel Consistories, the local nobility, by order of the Governor-General, and for the City Consistories of Riga and Reval, the Magistrates of these cities, elect from among themselves two candidates for each place; for clerical Assessors of all these Consistories, each proposes to the clergy of its district — Livonia, Estonia, and Courland four, and Ösel, Riga, and Reval three — candidates from among them. Of these the clergy elects two for each vacancy that has opened. Upon completion of the election, this is reported to the Governor-General, who communicates it to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, stating his opinion of the candidates presented to him. The Ministry of Internal Affairs confirms one of these candidates; regarding clerical Assessors it requests beforehand the opinion of the General Consistory.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 294; 1847 Jul. 29 (21450).

438. The Chancelleries of the Consistories of St. Petersburg, Livonia, Estonia, Courland, and Moscow consist, each, of a Secretary, a Notary, and clerical staff, in accordance with the staff establishment. — The Notaries of the St. Petersburg and Moscow Consistories also perform the duties of Translators. — The Chancellery of the Courland Consistory has a separate Translator. — The Chancellery of the Ösel Consistory consists of a Secretary and one clerical staff member. — The written business of the Riga and Reval Consistories is conducted by the clerical officials of the Magistrates.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 295; 1847 Jul. 29 (21450).

439. To fill vacancies of Secretaries and Notaries in the Consistories of St. Petersburg, Livonia, Estonia, Courland, Moscow, and Ösel, these Consistories select persons versed in jurisprudence, and submit the Secretaries for confirmation by the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and the Notaries for confirmation by the General Consistory; the other clerical staff they appoint themselves.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 296.

440. The Secretaries of the Consistories, in performing their official duties, follow the general regulations concerning the office of Secretary.

*Ibid., § 297.*

441. Presidents, members, Secretaries, and other clerical officials of the Consistories, upon entering office, are brought in the established manner to an oath of allegiance in the service. To the ordinary formula thereof, the President, Vice-President, and other members of the Consistory add the following words: "I also swear before the Lord God and His Holy Gospel that in the discharge of the office of (such-and-such) entrusted to me, I shall, to the best of my ability and understanding and with a clear conscience, fulfill both the general laws of the state and the special statutes of the Evangelical Lutheran Church, so help me the Lord God."

*Ibid., § 298. DOCUMENTS_______________________________________ ____________________________________ 341*

442. To the offices of Presidents, secular Assessors, and other members of the St. Petersburg, Livonia, Estonia, Courland, Moscow, and Ösel Consistories are assigned ranks, set out in detail in the Statute on Civil Service (Book I).

*Ibid., § 299; 1835 Nov. 20 (8594); 1847 Jul. 23 (31434 [21434]); Jul. 29 (21450).*

443. Presidents, members, Secretaries, and other clerical officials are, on the basis of the general laws of the state, dismissed by the authority that confirmed them in their office.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 300.

444. The Evangelical Lutheran Consistories, each within the district of its jurisdiction, are obliged to see to it that the Evangelical Lutheran clergy and all persons subordinate to them, in their relations to the Church, conform all their actions precisely both to the general laws of the state and to the provisions of this Church Statute and the Instruction (Nakaz) pertaining to it (see Part II) and the Agenda (Art. 140, note). On this basis, the sphere of activity of the Consistories includes:

1) Oversight of the preservation of the purity of the doctrine of the Evangelical Lutheran Church, founded on Holy Scripture and expounded in the Symbolical Books of this Church, and likewise of the order of the conduct of worship and the administration of the sacraments and other rites, in accordance with the rules prescribed in the Church Agenda.

2) Supervision both of the discharge of office and, in general, of the conduct and manner of life of Preachers, as well as of candidates of the clergy present in their districts.

3) The protection and defense of the rights of the Church, the clergy, and church servants, and intercession on their behalf before higher authority.

4) The assignment of texts for preaching on the occasions specified in Articles 141, 676-678.

5) Preliminary review of church, dogmatic, homiletic, and other books of religious content of the Evangelical Lutheran confession, on the basis of the censorship regulations.

6) Authorization to establish private prayer meetings, on the basis of the rules established above in Chapter Two.

<...>

8) General supervision of the instruction of Evangelical Lutheran youth in the Law of God, both in state and private educational institutions.

9) Review and adjudication in the first instance of all cases concerning betrothal, the publication of banns, or the contracting and dissolution of marriages, on the basis of the provisions set forth above, in Chapter Four.

10) Examination of candidates, both for obtaining the right to preach (pro venia concionandi) and for admission as Preachers (pro ministerio), as well as spiritual interviews with them (colloquium) in cases prescribed by the provisions of Chapter Five and the Instruction to the clergy set out below (see Part II).

11) The ordination and induction into office of newly appointed Preachers; representation to the Ministry of Internal Affairs concerning candidates for Preacher vacancies, and the filling of these vacancies when this is granted to them by the provisions of this Statute.

12) Representation to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, through the General Consistory, concerning persons elected to the rank of Provosts on the basis of the provisions of Chapter Six of this Statute, and arrangements for the discharge of the Provost's office pending the election and confirmation of a new Provost.

13) The issuance to newly appointed Provosts and Preachers of letters of induction (Constitutorium), and the announcement of the appointment of a new Provost to all Preachers of his district.

14) Representation to the Ministry of Internal Affairs concerning the dismissal of Preachers and Provosts entirely from office, or their leave of absence for more than twenty-eight days.

15) Authorization for Preachers to assume the duties of guardians, on the basis of the provisions of Chapter Five of this Statute.

16) The investigation and settlement of disputed matters between Preachers of different parishes, or between them and their Adjuncts or parishioners, on subjects belonging to the ecclesiastical department.

17) The investigation of complaints against Provosts, Superintendents, and General Superintendents, and the submission of their findings thereon for consideration by the General Consistory.

18) Review and adjudication of cases concerning negligence and offenses in office of all clergy belonging to their district.

19) Oversight to ensure that persons of clerical rank accused of criminal offenses are tried in the secular courts only in the presence of a deputy from the clergy, and the appointment of such deputies to the appropriate secular court; the removal from office of clergy committed for criminal trial or under investigation, and their dismissal or expulsion from clerical rank, pursuant to a sentence that has entered into legal force.

20) Recommendations for awards to persons serving in their department: for clergy through the General Consistory, and for secular persons directly to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

21) Oversight of the exact execution of the rules established in Chapters Six and Nine of this Statute concerning church visitations and Evangelical Lutheran Synods, and, when necessary, the drawing up of special instructions for Provosts, Superintendents, and General Superintendents for these visitations; drafts of these instructions are submitted for consideration by the General Consistory and confirmation by the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

22) Representations to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, through the General Consistory, concerning the construction of new churches, the establishment of new parishes and filial churches, and permission for voluntary collections of donations for this purpose.

23) Representations to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, through the General Consistory, concerning the establishment of new Provostships, and the granting of new patronage rights.

24) The imposition, by order of higher authority, of church penance on persons sentenced thereto by judgment.

25) General oversight of the funds existing in their districts for the assistance of Pastors' widows and orphans, and the promotion of the establishment and extension of such funds.

26) Special authorizations left by the provisions of this Statute to the discretion and authority of the Consistory.

*Ibid. § 301. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 343*

445. It is furthermore made the duty of the Consistories:

1) To submit, both to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and to the General Consistory, brief service records of the Provosts and Preachers subordinate to them and conduct records (kondouite lists) of the candidates of the clergy present in their district, lists submitted by the General Superintendents and Superintendents to the Consistories, and together with these the lists of the President, the clerical Vice-President, and the other members and officials of the Chancelleries. These lists are submitted annually in February. In compiling those concerning secular persons serving in the Consistory, the ordinary form established for the service records of civil officials is observed; the service and conduct records of the clergy are compiled according to a special form (a).

Note. In the service records of the Presidents of the Evangelical Lutheran Consistories submitted to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the assessments of them are made by the Heads of Governorates, with the sole exception of the President of the St. Petersburg Consistory, who is assessed by the President of the Evangelical Lutheran General Consistory; all other persons, both secular and clerical, of the Consistories, as well as the officials of the Consistorial Chancelleries, are assessed by the Presidents of the Consistories. The lists are confirmed by the signature of the same person who makes the assessment (b).

2) Submission to the General Consistory (likewise in February of each year) of a register of all births, deaths, and marriages that occurred in the preceding year within the jurisdiction of the Consistory, according to the form given for this purpose.

3) Submission to the General Consistory of special registers, according to established forms, of cases that were pending in the Consistory and not concluded in the course of the year, and of documents completed and not completed. These registers are submitted in January of each year, and indicate specifically which cases remain unconcluded.

4) Submission to the General Consistory of detailed reports on the state of church affairs in their districts, on notable occurrences relating thereto, on the manner in which the clergy discharge their duties, on the conduct of worship and their other labors, on the most important arrangements made in the course of the year, on investigations conducted into Preachers, on progress in the instruction of youth in the Law of God, and so forth. These reports are submitted at the end of November each year; to them the Consistories append registers (according to the form given for that purpose) on the number of churches and clergy under their jurisdiction, as well as on all persons confirmed in the course of the year, beginning from October 1.

5) Submission to the General Consistory, annually by November 1, of a list of all members and officials of the Consistory for inclusion in the Address Calendar.

6) Submission to the General Consistory of lists of holders of orders under the jurisdiction of the Consistories, according to the rules and forms established in the Statute on Orders.

7) Submission to the Treasury Chambers, not later than February 1 of each year, of accounts of monetary sums disbursed from the state treasury or received on its account, together with the bound ledgers for the auditing of these accounts.

Note. In the monthly verifications of funds, the Consistories are guided by the special rules of accounting established for the Department of Spiritual Affairs of Foreign Confessions (c).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 302, item 1; 1852 Jan. 28 (25944) Art. 143, item 4. - (b) 1834 Jul. 19 (7287). — (c) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 302, items 2—7 and note; see Statute on Orders, Arts. 263, 264, and the Accounting Statute of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

446. The Consistories of St. Petersburg, Moscow, Riga, and Reval hold two, or at least one, sessions per week; the Consistories of Livonia, Estonia, Courland, and Ösel gather for full sessions (juridiques) twice a year; at other times, for the conduct of current business, three members remain: two secular and one clerical, or two clerical and one secular. The days of sessions and the dates for the juridiques are appointed in advance. For urgent matters admitting no delay, ordinary meetings or juridiques are convened immediately, as needed.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 303.

447. Consistories that do not hold full weekly meetings transact, in their ordinary (permanent) sessions, generally only less important, current business; the more important matters are subject to the review of the full Consistorial assemblies, including exclusively the following:

1) All general measures concerning the whole clergy of the Consistorial district.

2) Proposals for changes in any part of the church structure and representations thereon to higher authority.

3) Representations concerning the filling of Provost and Preacher vacancies, when this depends on the Consistories, as well as concerning the appointment of their own clerical members, the Secretary, and the Notary. In case of necessity, Consistories may request in writing the votes of absent members.

4) All authorizations which, by virtue of this Statute, the Consistory has the right to grant without confirmation by higher authority.

5) The decision of all judicial and divorce cases.

*Ibid., § 304.*

448. The Consistories communicate with the Ministry of Internal Affairs and with the General Consistory by reports and representations, and from them receive proposals and decrees; communications with provincial offices, Church Councils, Colleges, Conventions, and Trusteeships, as well as with General Superintendents and Superintendents, are conducted by communications; to subordinate Provosts and Preachers the Consistories give instructions, and from them receive reports and representations.

Note. Reports and representations to the Ministry of Internal Affairs and to the General Consistory must always be signed by all members present at the sitting of the Consistories.

*Ibid., § 305.*

449. Business is conducted in the Consistories in the German language; petitions, as well as all other incoming documents, must be in Russian or German.

Note. Reports of the St. Petersburg and Moscow Consistories to the Ministry of Internal Affairs must be in Russian; the other Consistories may use the German language.

*Ibid., § 306.*

450. Monetary sums accumulated in the Consistories from exactions under imposed fines, or for improper appeals, and from any other income of this kind, are converted into funds for Preachers' widows and orphans. The Consistories report on this annually to the General Consistory.

*Ibid., § 307. DOCUMENTS______________________________________ _____________________________________ 345*

451. All Evangelical Lutheran Consistories have their own seals with the inscription: seal of the Evangelical Lutheran N Consistory. All their packets sent under this seal are dispatched without payment of postage fees.

*Ibid., § 308.*

Section Two.

On the General Consistory.

452. The Evangelical Lutheran General Consistory is composed of a secular President, a clerical Vice-President, two secular and two clerical members of the Evangelical Lutheran confession.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 309.

453. The President and Vice-President of the General Consistory are appointed by His Imperial Majesty.

*Ibid., § 310.*

454. For the places of secular members, the Livonia, Estonia, and Ösel Landrat Colleges, the Courland Oberhofgericht, the Riga and Reval City Magistrates, and the St. Petersburg and Moscow Consistories; and for the places of clerical members, all the Consistories — present candidates, each of these bodies one each; the Landrat Colleges, the Courland Oberhofgericht, and the City Magistrates through the Governor-General of the Baltic governorates, and the Consistories directly to the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Each Consistory is obliged to choose its candidates from among the Pastors of its own district. — The Minister, having weighed the opinions expressed by the Governors-General and the Consistories, and having, moreover, requested the opinion of the General Consistory regarding candidates for clerical membership, submits them with his own conclusion for the Highest consideration.

*Ibid., § 311; 1845 Jun. 18 (19109).*

455. Both secular and clerical members of the General Consistory are appointed for three years. Upon the expiration of this term, new elections are held and candidates presented according to the procedure established in Article 454; but each of the bodies named therein may elect and present a person who has already previously been a candidate or member.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 312.

456. Attached to the General Consistory is a Procurator, appointed under the general rules concerning Procurators.

*Ibid., § 313; cf. Statutes on Civil Service, Book 1.*

457. The Chancellery of the General Consistory is composed of a Secretary, his Assistant, a Controller, a Translator, an Executor (who is at the same time Archivist and Treasurer), and the necessary number of clerical staff, according to the establishment. — The Secretary is appointed, upon the representation of the General Consistory, by the Ministry of Internal Affairs; his Assistant and the other officials and clerical staff by the General Consistory itself.

Note. It is the duty of the Controller to be in charge of the accounting section of the Consistory in general, and in particular the audit of accounts relating to the administration of the properties of the churches subordinate to it, and the compilation, in this regard, of registers submitted annually to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 314; 1837 Apr. 10 (10119).

458. To the President and the other secular members of the General Consistory, as well as to the officials of its Chancellery, are assigned ranks of office and pension categories on the basis of the Statutes on Civil Service (Books I and III) [(a)]. — To the clerical members of the General Consistory is assigned the rank of Ober-Consistorial Councillors (Ober-Consistorialräthe) and the title Hochehrwürden, and to the Vice-President the title Hochehrwürden [(b)]; moreover the Vice-President wears on his breast the cross granted to him under the rule of Article 428, placed upon him upon his induction into office by the President (c).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 315; 1837 Apr. 10 (10119); 1841 Jun. 27 (14693); Jul. 2 (14708). — (b) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 315. — (c) 1833 Jun. 3, Highest Command.

459. The President and members of the General Consistory, as well as the officials of its Chancellery, are permitted to hold other positions, retaining their salary, provided that the duties combined with them do not interfere with their work in the General Consistory.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 316; 1833 Nov. 4 (6547).

460. The sphere of activity of the General Consistory includes:

1) The review of all judicial cases pending in the Evangelical Lutheran Consistories and submitted to the General Consistory on appeal or by private complaint.

2) Oversight of the actions of the Consistories, as well as of the General Superintendents and Superintendents in general, and the review of complaints against the Consistories or their members concerning the administration of church affairs.

3) Oversight of the order of administration of the properties of the Evangelical Lutheran churches. — All private capitals of these churches are subject to accounting by the General Consistory.

4) Approval of texts proposed by local Consistories in place of the customary ones (Pericopen), and approval of collections of hymns for use in worship (Arts. 141 and 146).

5) Authorizations for marriages in the cases specified above, in Articles 207 and 213.

6) Arrangements for the induction of General Superintendents and Superintendents into office.

7) The review of complaints by patrons regarding the non-confirmation by any local Consistory of a candidate elected by them.

8) The review of complaints by candidates of the clergy against decisions of Consistories concerning their appointment as Preachers.

9) The expression of opinion on matters which, on the basis of the provisions of this Statute, pass from the local Consistories to the General Consistory, for submission to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

10) The review of cases forwarded to the General Consistory by the Ministry of Internal Affairs for its opinion.

11) Representations to the Ministry of Internal Affairs concerning the convening of the Evangelical Lutheran General Synod and the designation of matters and proposals to be discussed therein.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 317; 1850 Nov. 7 (24608).

461. The General Consistory, in administrative matters, is subordinate to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and in judicial matters to the Governing Senate, on the

DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 347

same basis on which all the higher judicial bodies are subordinate to it; excepted from this are only:

1) Divorce cases coming from local Consistories, by complaint or appeal, to the General Consistory, and in which it decides finally whether the marital union is to be dissolved (quoad vinculum).

2) Cases concerning departures from the doctrine of the Evangelical Lutheran Church, or from the rules of worship and rites. In cases of this kind, the General Consistory presents its conclusions to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, for report to His Imperial Majesty.

3) Cases concerning the deprivation of rank and the removal or temporary suspension from office of Preachers and other clerical dignitaries, upon complaints submitted for review by the General Consistory.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 318.

462. The General Consistory reports to the Ministry of Internal Affairs on all cases in which it is necessary to seek the Highest authorization of His Imperial Majesty, or in which measures of the Ministry are needed, as well as on matters requiring communication with other Ministries, Governors-General, Governors, and the chief heads of separate branches of state administration, also on disputes that may arise between this Consistory and the ecclesiastical departments of other confessions, and finally on doubts that arise as to whether or not some matter belongs to its jurisdiction.

*Ibid., § 319.*

463. Moreover the General Consistory submits annually to the Ministry of Internal Affairs:

1) In February, the service records of its President, Vice-President, members, and officials of the Chancellery. — The lists of secular persons are submitted according to the general form established for civil officials, and those of clerical members according to a special form given for this purpose.

Note. The service record of the President of the General Consistory is submitted to the Ministry without assessment, but under the signature of the Vice-President and all clerical and secular members of this Consistory.

2) At the beginning of March, a general register, according to the established form, of all births, deaths, and marriages in the preceding year within the departments of all the Evangelical Lutheran Consistories, showing how many there were in each Consistorial district and how many in total.

3) At the beginning of February, a general register, according to the given forms, of cases pending and not concluded during the year both in the local Consistories and in the General Consistory, as well as of documents completed and not completed, showing how many cases have been concluded, how many remain unresolved, and which ones specifically.

4) At the beginning of December, a detailed report on the state of church affairs in all the Consistorial districts, on the basis of the reports of the local Consistories submitted to the General Consistory (Art. 445, item 4), together with a general register, according to the form given for that purpose, of the number of churches and clergy, as well as of all persons confirmed in the course of the year, beginning from October 1, for each Consistorial district separately and for all districts together.

5) In March, a general register of the state of the funds for Preachers' widows and orphans, and of the sums received into them during the year.

6) Likewise in March, a general table of the state of the property of the Evangelical Lutheran churches. — This table must contain a brief indication of all monetary sums received and expended in each church; to it is appended a special register of all fines and other monies of this kind received by the General Consistory and the other Consistories and Church Trusteeships, and of their use or intended use.

Note. Annual general lists of all clerical and secular members for the Address Calendar, information on holders of orders for the Chapter of Orders, and information on Protestants born, married, and deceased are sent, where appropriate, directly from the General Consistory.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 320; 1834 Jul. 19 (7287); 1852 Jan. 28 (25944) Arts. 132, 133, 143, item 5.

464. By February 1 of each year, the General Consistory is obliged to submit to the State Comptroller an account of the monetary sums disbursed for its maintenance.

Note. In the monthly verifications of sums, the General Consistory is guided by the rules of accounting established for the Department of Spiritual Affairs of Foreign Confessions (see the Accounting Statute of the Ministry of Internal Affairs).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 321.

465. The General Consistory operates on the right of a collegial institution. The order of the conduct of business therein, and the rights and duties of the members and officials of its Chancellery, are determined by the general rules for collegial bodies.

*Ibid., § 322, item 1.*

466. In the absence of the President and Vice-President, the senior of the secular members presides in the General Consistory.

*Ibid., § 322, item 2.*

467. The Procurator of the General Consistory acts on the basis of the general provisions concerning the office of Procurator. He also has oversight of matters of an administrative nature transacted in the General Consistory. In judicial matters the Procurator reports to the Ministry of Justice, and in other matters to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

*Ibid., § 323.*

468. Cases within the General Consistory itself and its correspondence with the offices subordinate to it shall be conducted in the German language. Petitions to the General Consistory may be submitted in either Russian or German. Reports to the Governing Senate and to the Ministry of Internal Affairs must be written in Russian; the enclosures accompanying such reports must always be accompanied by Russian translations.

*Ibid., § 324.*

469. The General Consistory shall decide the cases falling within its jurisdiction during two juridical terms, each of which must last not less than one month and not more than two; the first begins on January 15, the second on June 1 of each year.

*Ibid., § 325; 1843 May 26 (16891). DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 349*

470. During the juridical terms, the General Consistory shall meet, depending on the number of cases received, either daily or at least three times a week. Upon conclusion of the juridical terms, the members of the General Consistory are dismissed (a). For travel to St. Petersburg to attend the juridical terms, and back, the lay and clerical members of the General Consistory receive travel money (b).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 326. — (b) Ibid., staff regulations.

471. For cases arriving at the General Consistory at a time when there is no juridical term in session, and requiring the adoption of some preliminary measures, as well as for those cases which must be submitted to the Ministry of Internal Affairs without a special opinion, the President and Vice-President hold weekly sessions and make the appropriate arrangements; they likewise gather the necessary information and set deadlines for the appearance of petitioners or respondents. In the absence of the President or Vice-President, or when disagreement arises between them, an extraordinary lay or clerical member of the Evangelical Lutheran confession is appointed by the Ministry of Internal Affairs, for that occasion only.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 327.

472. Monetary sums accumulated in the General Consistory from collections on imposed fines or for improper appeals, and from other revenues of this kind, are sent annually, at its discretion and according to its allocation, to the funds for the widows and orphans of preachers.

*Ibid., § 328.*

473. The General Consistory has its own seal bearing the image of the state coat of arms and the inscription: seal of the Evangelical Lutheran General Consistory. All its packets bearing this seal are dispatched without payment of weight fees.

*Ibid., § 329.*

##### CHAPTER EIGHT.

On judicial proceedings in the Consistories.

Section One.

General provisions.

474. Only those cases which are expressly assigned to the consideration and decision of the Consistories, whether local or the General Consistory, by Articles 444, 460, and 461, are subject to their jurisdiction.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 330.

475. The jurisdiction of any Consistory in judicial matters may not be extended to cases falling under another Consistory or another court, even if a counterclaim on such a matter has been declared before it, or if one of the disputing parties, or even both by mutual agreement (consensu expresso vel tacito), should choose it to decide their case (prorogatio necessaria vel voluntaria).

*Ibid., § 331.*

476. The Consistories are required to forward to the appropriate secular offices even those judicial cases which, although subject to review by an ecclesiastical court, are so only in part and not in general; the secular courts, for their part, request the opinion of the appropriate Consistory regarding these matters.

*Ibid., § 332.*

477. When, owing to circumstances arising in a case, a police investigation or a criminal proceeding becomes necessary, the Consistory, without proceeding further with its own review of the matter, refers it to the appropriate secular office.

*Ibid., § 333.*

478. The rules concerning the principal and non-principal persons in a case and its adjudication (Haupt-Personen und Neben-Personen), concerning the various kinds of evidence, and concerning the order of proceedings, are to be strictly observed by the Consistories. In general, in all cases for which no special rules of procedure are established in this Statute, they are guided by the general laws, or by the local laws existing in the governorate in which each of them is located.

*Ibid., § 334.*

479. To expedite proceedings both in private matters and in those arising from accusations against clergy for violation of their duties, and in general in complaints against their official conduct, the Consistory sets, for all persons connected with the case, deadlines for appearance, submission of explanations, and performance of other duties in the conduct of the case, but not more than three in each individual instance: the first and second under threat of incurring, for missing them, the established fine (termini poenales); the third under threat of forfeiting the right to perform the act for which the deadline was set (praeclusio). Exceptions to this rule are permitted only in divorce cases, on the basis of the provisions of Article 529.

*Ibid., § 335.*

480. In setting deadlines, the Consistory takes into consideration both the circumstances of the case and the greater or lesser distance of the places where those summoned to appear or to perform other duties in the conduct of the case are located, strictly observing the rules established for this purpose by the general laws.

*Ibid., § 336.*

481. For missing the first deadline without lawful cause, the Consistory imposes, at its discretion, a fine of from three to seven rubles fifty kopecks in silver, and for a similar failure to meet the second deadline, double that amount, while also granting the other disputing party, in private matters, the right to seek, through the appropriate secular court, compensation for losses caused by such non-appearance. If the guilty party is unable to pay the fine imposed on him, he is punished by temporary confinement of from three to twelve days.

*Ibid., § 337; 1839 Nov. 9 (12867). DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 351*

482. If, before the expiration of the appointed deadline, a request for postponement (dilatio) is submitted, together with the presentation of proper certification of the reality and legality of the reasons for which such postponement is requested, the Consistory may, at its discretion, extend the deadlines it has set by three days, or by a week, or finally by as much as two weeks, but no more. Such postponements in private matters may be granted by the Consistories, without hearing the opposing party, no more than twice. For a third postponement, as well as for the first or second when it is proposed to extend the appointed deadline beyond two weeks, the Consistory grants its consent only for the most important reasons and only after first hearing the explanation of the other party.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 338.

483. Persons required to appear before the Consistory during the conduct of a case, or their attorneys, are served with summonses (citationes) to appear before the Consistory, at its discretion, either through its own officers or through the appropriate local authorities. In the same manner, the other orders of the Consistory in judicial matters are conveyed to whomever they concern.

*Ibid., § 339.*

484.
