The estates of these manors (cl. 2) are obliged to collect the portions apportioned to the peasants belonging to them, semi-annually, without any arrears, and to pay them directly into the Chief Church Wardenships, together with their own contributions (b).

(a) Ibid., § 493. — (b) 1837 Mar. 8 (10066).

644. Chief Church Wardenships exercise oversight over the Church Wardens and over all church affairs under the direct administration of the latter. They ensure that church property is administered properly, safeguarded from all harm and loss, and increased as far as possible; that churches and church buildings are in proper order, and that those charged with overseeing this perform their duty diligently and precisely; that, at a very close distance from the church, no new buildings or establishments are erected whose proximity might either endanger it in case of fire, or hinder divine services.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 494, cl. 1.

645. Chief Church Wardenships are to assemble annually, at the appointment of the President, for deliberation, and to conduct private visitations to the churches of their districts, in order to verify the inventories kept there, to inspect the church buildings, and all property belonging to the churches.

*Ibid., § 494, cl. 2.*

646. The Chief Church Wardenships are charged with the principal oversight of the church police, whose duties in particular include ensuring that the roads leading to the churches are kept in good order.

*Ibid., § 494, cl. 3.*

647. At the end of the year they submit to the General Consistory a report on their activities and a general statement of the receipts and expenditures of monetary sums of the churches of their district.

*Ibid., § 494, cl. 4.*

648. In general, the Chief Church Wardenships are obliged, in their activities, to be guided by the regulations and procedures existing for this purpose in Livland governorate, insofar as the special local circumstances in other governorates permit.

*Ibid., § 494, cl. 5.*

649. In Kurland governorate, the relations of the Chief Church Wardenships with the other government offices of this governorate, pending a special instruction, are conducted according to the following provisions: to the Provincial Board, the Ober-Hofgericht, and the Chambers, they submit reports and receive decrees from them; to the Church Wardenships they issue instructions and receive submissions from them; complaints against any and all orders of the Chief Church Wardenships are brought to the Provincial Boards within a period of four weeks from the day such orders are announced; the Provincial Boards resolve these complaints only in undisputed matters, while in case of dispute they refer them to the consideration of the appropriate judicial bodies.

1837 Jun. 30 (10407); 1840 Dec. 16 (14055).

650. The rights and duties of the Church Inspections in Mitau, Bauske, Goldingen, and Windau, and of the Town Magistrates in Riga, Reval, Dorpat, Pernau, Arensburg, Libau, and Narva, in respect of the management of church economic affairs, remain on the same footing as existed before 1832. — Matters of this kind in the Saratov Office of Foreign Settlers and in the Guardianship Committee for Foreign Settlers of the Southern Region are to be managed only in the presence of an ecclesiastical member, who is appointed for this purpose to each of these bodies by the General Consistory, upon the recommendation of the local Consistories. — With respect to church economic affairs, the Saratov Office of Foreign Settlers and the Guardianship Committee for Foreign Settlers of the Southern Region act on the basis of the rules established for the Chief Church Trusteeships in the preceding articles. These bodies, as well as the Church Inspections in Mitau, Bauske, Goldingen, and Windau, and the Magistrates of the towns of Riga, Reval, Dorpat, Pernau, Arensburg, Libau, and Narva, are obliged, at the end of each year, to submit to the General Consistory a report on their activities in the administration of economic affairs and a general statement of the income and expenditure of the sums of the churches of their districts (a). Only persons belonging to the Evangelical Lutheran confession may be elected as members of Church Inspections (b).

(a) 1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 495. — (b) 1842 Oct. 19 (16097).

651. Disputes arising between Preachers and Church Trusteeships concerning their mutual duties and rights are subject to review either by the authorities immediately superior to the Church Trusteeships, if the matter concerns arrangements of an economic nature, or else by the local Consistory.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 496.

Third Section.

On Church Buildings.

652. When it is necessary to rebuild or newly construct a church, the Trustees submit a report on this, as appropriate, to the Chief Church Trusteeship, the Magistrate, the Church Inspection, or the colonial authority, and these bodies communicate this to the proper Consistory for submission, with its opinion, to the General Consistory. In parishes whose economic affairs are managed by Church Councils, Collegia, or Convents, these bodies communicate the need to rebuild or newly construct a church directly to the local Consistory, for submission to the General Consistory. If the General Consistory, having weighed the means and needs of the parish, itself recognizes that the proposed construction is necessary, it submits the matter for the decision of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. This same procedure is observed also in the case where a parish requests assistance for repairs to a church, or authorization to establish a collection of voluntary contributions for this purpose. However, repairs to churches and the construction of replacements for churches that have become dilapidated or have been destroyed by some occurrence may also be authorized by the ecclesiastical authorities themselves (see above, art. 125).

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 497; 1856 Dec. 10 (31240).

653. In the preparation and review of plans and elevations for Evangelical Lutheran churches, and in the execution of the construction itself, the rules of the Building Code must be strictly observed.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 498; 1845 Aug. 15 (19283) arts. 1350-1352.

654. Upon completion of the construction of a church, the Trustees, or the Church Councils, Collegia, or Convents, following the procedure specified in article 652, bring this to the attention of the local Consistory, which makes the necessary arrangements for the consecration of the church, on the basis of the provisions of the Liturgical Agenda.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 499.

655. Reports on actions taken in the course of construction are submitted by Church Trustees, for auditing, to their immediate superior authority, while Church Councils, Collegia, or Convents submit them directly to the General Consistory.

*Ibid., § 500.*

656. All bodies administering church property each have their own special seal, and packages sent under this seal are exempt from the payment of postal weight fees.

*Ibid., § 501.*

##### CHAPTER ELEVEN.

On the Right of Patronage.

657. If one or several members of some Evangelical Lutheran society wish to erect anew a church of this confession, on condition that the right of patronage over it be granted to them, a submission on this matter is made following the procedure prescribed in article 652.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 502.

658. The right of patronage is acquired by: 1) the free cession of a site for the church and the parsonage buildings belonging to it; 2) the construction of the church at one's own expense; 3) the construction of a parsonage and the designation of sufficient lands or sums for the maintenance of a Preacher; 4) the complete restoration of a ruined church in which divine service could no longer be performed.

*Ibid., § 503.*

659. The right of patronage acquired in this manner is confirmed by the Supreme Authority.

*Ibid., § 504.*

660. The right of patronage in the Evangelical Lutheran church, if it is not attached to an estate, is hereditary; but in every case it may be exercised only by a person professing the Christian faith (a). — In the Baltic governorates, owners of immovable estates who, by virtue of these estates or by inheritance, enjoy the right of patronage, but do not belong to the Evangelical Lutheran confession, are permitted, in the selection of a Preacher, either to exercise this right themselves, or to transfer it, by powers of attorney, to other persons of this confession, or to the local Consistories; if any of them fails to exercise this right within a period of six months from the opening of the vacancy for a Preacher, the Consistory itself appoints a Preacher at its own discretion, on the basis of article 189 of this Statute, but these same owners do not take part in Church Convents in the deliberation of matters that are purely ecclesiastical (b).

(a) Ibid., § 505. — (b) 1845 Aug. 21 (19130).

661. The right of patronage attached to the ownership of an estate, in the parish of which the church is located, passes to the new owner upon the cession or sale of this estate. Upon the granting of state-owned estates into perpetual and hereditary possession, the right of patronage attached to them likewise passes to the owner; but when an estate is granted only for lifetime possession or for a fixed term, this right is retained by the Treasury.

1832 Dec. 28 (5870) § 506.

662. In the division of an estate to which the right of patronage is attached, the parties participating in this division may confer this right, together with all the duties and privileges attached to it, upon one of the participants, of their choosing and with his consent. Such agreements are confirmed by the proper government offices in the ordinary manner, and are brought to the notice of the Ministry of Internal Affairs through the local and General Consistory.

*Ibid., § 507.*

663. If the person to whom the right of patronage belongs has not yet attained legal majority, or has been removed from the administration of the estate on account of insanity or other cause, then the guardian or trustee appointed over him exercises this right in his place. During bankruptcy proceedings over an estate to which the right of patronage is attached, the Consistory takes the place of the patron.

*Ibid., § 508.*

664. Together with the right of patronage, all the honorary privileges and special duties attached to it also pass to the new holder.

*Ibid., § 509.*

665. A patron is deprived of the right of patronage: 1) if it is proven that he appointed Preachers for money, or for other impermissible self-interested motives; 2) if it is proven that he has deliberately appropriated church property for himself, or has otherwise violated the rights of the Church; 3) if, more than three times in succession, not owing to absence but solely through negligence, he has failed to exercise the right of patronage belonging to him; finally, 4) if the church, the maintenance of which was entrusted to his care, has fallen into such ruin that divine service can no longer be performed in it. In the first three cases, the right of patronage passes, for the duration of his life, to the parish, and upon his death to his lawful heirs; in the last case, it passes to whoever restores the ruined church at his own expense.

*Ibid., § 510.*

666. The review of cases concerning the deprivation of anyone's rights of patronage belongs to the secular courts, but before rendering a decision on this they are obliged to seek the opinion of the ecclesiastical authorities.

*Ibid., § 511.*

667. Disputes as to who holds the right of patronage in a parish are examined in the first instance by the Chief Church Trusteeships and equivalent bodies administering church economic affairs; they attempt to reconcile the disputing parties; but in case of failure they refer the formal adjudication of such disputes to the proper secular courts as well.

*Ibid., § 512.*

##### CHAPTER TWELVE.

Instruction to the Clergy and Authorities

of the Evangelical Lutheran Church in the Empire.

I. On Doctrine.

668. The Evangelical Lutheran Consistories, General Superintendents, Superintendents, and Provosts are obliged, in the districts under their jurisdiction, to observe strictly that the doctrine of their Church be preserved and professed in all DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 383

its purity and in accordance with the Symbolic Books recognized by it (art. 134); they must, by every means and in every instance, endeavor to ensure that the clergy subordinate to them preach and expound the word of God entirely in accordance with the rules of the Church, in no way deviating from them or spreading opinions contrary to them. If it comes to the attention of Provosts, or of Superintendents or General Superintendents, that certain Preachers are expressing opinions deviating from the doctrine of the Church, they are obliged first to try to restrain them only by gentle admonitions inspired by Christian love, and, by resolving all their doubts through precise explanations grounded in Holy Scripture, to turn them onto the path of truth.

1832 Dec. 28 (5871) § 1.

669. If it comes to the attention of an Evangelical Lutheran Consistory that within its district a work is circulating among readers that contains an openly hostile disparagement of the dogmas of the faith professed by the Evangelical Lutheran Church, and that is liable to cause general offense among its members, then, after careful examination and consideration of this information, it must report this to the General Consistory. This report must include, in addition to a copy of the accused book, an opinion of the Consistory grounded in precise evidence, indicating those passages of the work that are worthy of censure, and, if necessary, the words of Holy Scripture and the explanations of the Symbolic Books that are improperly refuted in this work. The General Consistory submits this, together with its opinion, for the consideration of the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

*Ibid., § 2.*

670. The Evangelical Lutheran Consistories, General Superintendents, Superintendents, and Provosts must carefully ensure that the clergy subordinate to them, and, insofar as it depends on them, the secular persons within the districts under their jurisdiction, in no way permit themselves to disturb, in any manner whatsoever, the good harmony with the other religions freely existing within the state, and that they do not, whether by words or by any other means, induce persons professing another faith to convert to their Church. Preachers must decline the requests of those who, belonging to another confession equally protected within the state, ask to be instructed in the dogmas of the Evangelical Lutheran confession, or to have some religious rite performed for them, still less to be received into the bosom of the Evangelical Lutheran Church. Proper authorization for this (art. 6) may lawfully be sought only by the persons of foreign confessions themselves who wish to change their faith, and without any involvement of the clergy (*). <...>

(*) This does not apply to persons belonging to various Evangelical Protestant confessions: Preachers may perform religious rites for them. For conversion from one Evangelical Protestant confession to another, it is sufficient for those wishing to do so to present certificates from the Preachers of their former parishes attesting to their expressed intention. Preachers who receive them, on the basis of such certificates, into another Protestant confession are obliged to report every such conversion, through the local Consistory, to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

*Ibid., § 3 <...>.*

II. On Divine Service and Special Sacred Rites.

671. The Consistories, General Superintendents, Superintendents, and Provosts are obliged to observe strictly that in the churches of the districts under their jurisdiction public divine service is performed on all Sundays, feast days, and other days especially designated for that purpose (arts. 142, 143), and that in doing so the rules of the Church Agenda (art. 140) are precisely observed.

1832 Dec. 28 (5871) § 4.

672. If it should prove necessary to make some changes in the Liturgical provisions (art. 140), the local Consistories, after prior discussion at Evangelical Lutheran Synods, submit this matter, through the General Consistory, to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

*Ibid., § 5; 1847 Jul. 29 (21450).*

673. The Consistories, General Superintendents, Superintendents, and Provosts must also observe, in the districts under their jurisdiction, that all the special pious customs existing in some places during divine service continue to be preserved as before (Dec. 28, 1832) — during the reading of the prayers before the altar, or the Lord's Prayer: Our Father, the Gospel, the Apostolic Epistles, the words of Confession and the Institution of Holy Communion, or during the singing of collects, hymns of praise and of the faith, during the announcement from the pulpit of the words of the text, and during the church blessing, and so forth.

1832 Dec. 28 (5871) § 6.

674. If a parish and its Preacher find it necessary to alter or altogether abolish any of the special customs existing in it during divine service, they must seek authorization for this from the local Consistory, which reports its decisions on this matter without delay, through the General Consistory, to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, explaining also the reasons that prompted it.

*Ibid., § 7.*

675. The Consistories, General Superintendents, Superintendents, and Provosts are obliged to impress upon Preachers that they should pay special attention to preaching, as one of the most important parts of Evangelical Lutheran divine service, and that they should undertake the delivery of their sermons only after due preparation through prayer and reflection; that their discourses should be filled with the true life-giving teaching of Christ the Savior, in all its purity and integrity, and not with useless speculations; that the text for the sermon should truly serve as the foundation of the sermon and be interpreted and applied correctly, in accordance with its direct meaning; finally, that Preachers, both in the clarity and precision of their language and in the manner of their delivery, should be equally comprehensible to the learned and the unlearned, and equally edifying to all. The mere reading (Ablesen) of sermons is not permitted. The Consistories and other ecclesiastical authorities are also to observe that Preachers, in their discourses, entirely avoid inappropriate discussions of matters unrelated to religion, especially contemporary political events and measures adopted by the government in connection with them, and that they permit themselves no reproachful expressions concerning other faiths and peoples. If a Preacher considers it necessary to draw special attention DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 385

and censure to vices that have grown prevalent in his parish, or to dangerous religious errors, then, in fulfilling this duty, he is likewise obliged to avoid every form of bias or personal displeasure, indicating or even hinting at no one by name, so that the result of his admonitions may be, not murmuring, hatred, or discord, but sincere recognition of the error, repentance, and correction.

*Ibid., § 8.*

676. Although the Sunday and feast-day pericopes (selected passages from Holy Scripture) currently (Dec. 28, 1832) in use should generally serve as the basis of morning sermons, nevertheless, in order to acquaint listeners more fully with the entire content of Holy Scripture, the local Consistories may, on occasion, with the authorization of the General Consistory, designate other pericopes for use during the year (art. 141). The texts for days of penitence, commemoration of the departed, the harvest festival, and the consecration of a church (art. 142) are designated by the local Consistories at their own discretion, while that for the day of the celebration of the Reformation (ibid.) is designated by the General Consistory, with the confirmation of the Ministry of Internal Affairs. Preachers are not forbidden to preach sermons also on pericopes of feast days not specified in article 142, and, in extraordinary cases, to select texts from Holy Scripture for their sermons themselves, reporting this to the local Consistory.

*Ibid., § 9.*

677. The Consistories are obliged to see to it that evening sermons, where these are established, are devoted predominantly, over the course of one year, to the explanation of texts from the Apostolic Epistles, and in the following year to the exposition of Luther's Catechism, except for the season of Lent, which is set aside for contemplation of the sufferings of our Lord Jesus Christ. Where there are no evening sermons, this may, with the authorization of the Consistory, form the subject of some of the morning sermons.

*Ibid., § 10.*

678. On the basis of article 144, the Consistories, General Superintendents, Superintendents, and Provosts are obliged to see to it that, everywhere in the districts under their jurisdiction, special sermons and hours of prayer are established during the week, in addition to Sundays and feast days, if not throughout the entire year then at least for the season of Lent, and that in these sermons entire books of Holy Scripture are expounded in parts, simply, clearly, and thoroughly, and that during Lent chiefly the history of the Passion of our Lord is expounded. The local Consistories report their arrangements in this regard to the General Consistory.

*Ibid., § 11.*

679. Since congregational church singing, by lending greater solemnity to divine service, contributes to the arousal and elevation of devout feelings, the Consistories and other ecclesiastical authorities are charged with the absolute duty of ensuring that everywhere Preachers concern themselves with the gradual improvement of church singing, and especially among the youth attending school (Schuljugend). The General Superintendents, Superintendents, and Provosts must impress upon Preachers that, in choosing hymns and melodies, they should have regard to the intellectual and spiritual disposition of their parishioners, to the purpose of the celebration, and to other similar circumstances; that they should teach their parishioners to sing purely, simply, harmoniously, and melodiously, and, together with the Church Trustees and Elders, concern themselves with forming choirs of pupils and other parishioners; that ancient hymns should also sometimes be sung, such as, for example, Litanies, Te Deum Laudamus, and so forth; and finally, that as far as possible the voices of parishioners should everywhere be accompanied by organs, for which purpose Preachers and Church Trustees and Elders must strive to install instruments of this kind in all churches, taking care at the same time that organists play sacred melodies precisely according to the content of the Collection of Church Melodies (Choral-Buch) and in accordance with the spirit of church music.

*Ibid., § 12.*

680. In special cases, as for example when a parish has long had the custom of singing some sacred hymn, though it is not included in the Collection of sacred hymns used by it, or in the case of some extraordinary occurrence, the Consistories are granted the right to authorize the singing of sacred hymns not contained in the Collection, reporting this to the General Consistory.

*Ibid., § 13.*

681. The instructions and examinations in the knowledge of the Law of God (Catechisationen), so useful for the moral and spiritual education of parishioners and established in the Evangelical Lutheran Church since ancient times, must receive special attention from the Consistories and other ecclesiastical authorities. They are obliged to ensure that these catechizations are carefully carried out everywhere they existed before December 28, 1832, and are established, as far as possible, where they did not previously exist. In towns, catechizations may conveniently be combined with the evening service. In villages, where this is not possible, the Consistories are to encourage Preachers to conduct them in some other manner instead of catechizations in church. In the St. Petersburg and Baltic governorates, for instruction in the Law of God and for determining the degree of knowledge of it, Preachers must make use of the time of prayer or catechization journeys, or local visitation journeys (Local-Visitations-Fahrten).

*Ibid., § 14.*

682. The ecclesiastical authorities of the Baltic governorates are instructed to see to it that in the rural parishes of these governorates a special divine service in the German language is performed on feast days, on the day of general penitence, and generally whenever the parish expresses a wish for it, even if the number of German parishioners is quite small.

*Ibid., § 15.*

683. In towns, the main divine service is to begin at nine, or at the latest not later than ten o'clock. In villages it should be performed as early as possible, especially in winter, so as not to end too late and not to hinder the delivery of a sermon for another congregation, where this occurs.

*Ibid., § 16.*

684. In towns, divine service must begin in each church at one and the same hour, which is designated once and for all, either for all days generally or specifically for certain days.

*Ibid., § 17.*

685. In charitable institutions where a special divine service is performed, everything must remain as before (Dec. 28, 1832) with regard to both the beginning and the duration of the service. If it becomes necessary to alter, in this respect, a provision made by the founder of the charitable institution himself, the Consistory is obliged, after examining the circumstances of the matter, to submit this, through the General Consistory, to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

*Ibid., § 18.*

686. If congregations that hold divine service one after another in the same church cannot agree among themselves as to when the service of each of them should begin and end, their dispute is to be decided by the Consistory. Their agreements on this matter are also submitted to the General Consistory for its information.

*Ibid., § 19.*

687. The Consistories are to see to it that only such announcements are read from the pulpit as, by their content, may be accompanied by thanksgiving, prayer, doxology, or exhortation, or as are intended, by virtue of special Supreme commands or of instructions given by the higher local authority through the Consistories, for solemn proclamation from the pulpit. Other announcements are read from the lectern (von dem Pulte). Private matters must under no circumstances be announced in church.

*Ibid., § 20.*

688. The Consistories and other ecclesiastical authorities are obliged to see to the maintenance of good order in churches. Those who disturb it are, the first time, to be admonished, and, in case of continued defiance or of a new disturbance of order, especially one causing general offense, are to be handed over to the proper government office for proceedings against them according to law (Penal Code, arts. 235–252). The Consistories must impress upon Preachers that they should, by every possible means, contribute to establishing general reverence in churches, admonishing both the whole parish publicly and certain individuals privately, urging everyone to arrive at church in good time and not to leave it before the service is concluded; they must see to it that during the sermon all church doors are closed except one.

Note. Rules on church order in the colonies of foreigners are set forth in the Statute on Colonies (a). — In Reval, oversight of church policing and police arrangements in connection with church ceremonies, funerals, christenings, weddings, and so forth belong to the subjects under the jurisdiction of the Reval Magistrate (b).

(a) Ibid., § 21. — (b) Digest of Local Statutes of the Baltic (Ostsee) Governorates, Part I, art. 1014, item 10.

689. The Evangelical Lutheran Church has always regarded family or domestic divine service as one of the most effective means for preserving and strengthening piety in society, and therefore every father of a family and master of a household is granted the right, at his discretion, to establish domestic divine service for himself and his family and servants, provided only that this does not prevent them from attending public divine service. The Consistories, through the clergy subordinate to them, carefully observe this; in the event of any abuses, first the parish Preachers, and then the Consistories themselves, are obliged, by means of admonitions, to persuade the master of the household to put an end to the observed irregularities. If these measures prove unsuccessful, the Consistories report this to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, through the General Consistory.

1832 Dec. 28 (5871) § 22.

690. The right to permit private religious gatherings going beyond the bounds of ordinary domestic divine service belongs only to the local Consistories, which report the authorizations granted by them without delay, through the General Consistory, to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, notifying at the same time both the local civil authority and the Preacher in whose parish the private religious gathering being established is to take place. The Consistories permit the establishment of religious gatherings only to such persons as enjoy general respect in the parishes, have not been implicated in any unlawful acts or acts bringing shame and dishonor, are subjects of the Russian Empire, and are permanent residents of the place where they intend to hold the gatherings.

*Ibid., § 23.*

691. The Consistories are obliged, through the clergy subordinate to them, to observe carefully that in private religious gatherings the rules prescribed above in articles 149 and 150 are not violated. The parish Preachers, if they do not themselves lead these gatherings, must at least visit them as often as possible, to oversee everything taking place in them. If they discover any abuses or irregularities in these gatherings, they must try to put an end to them immediately, first by means of admonitions, and then by notifying the local Consistory, which, upon confirming the truth of the report, prohibits the gathering and announces the reasons for this to its participants through the parish Preacher. If, however, contrary to the Consistory's prohibition, the gatherings continue, it turns to the local authority, demanding that they be stopped and that those who fail to obey its instructions be punished.

*Ibid., § 24.*

692. Evangelical Lutheran Preachers, in everything concerning the performance of the sacraments and other church rites, conform precisely to the order established for their Church, observing at the same time the solemnity and dignity befitting their importance, instilling by their own example due reverence for these sacred institutions, and carefully removing everything that might hinder their salutary effect on the minds and hearts of those present. They are obliged, both in the performance of divine service and on all other occasions, diligently to explain to their parishioners the true meaning and purpose of the Church's institutions, admonishing them in particular not to attach to these sacred rites any superstitious customs or opinions, and not to allow themselves to use them for the attainment of any worldly advantages.

*Ibid., § 25.*

693. Holy baptism is to be performed even upon a malformed infant, provided only that it has a human form. In case of doubt, the Preacher is obliged to report this immediately to the proper Consistory and to the civil authority, which, after examination of the newborn by a physician, shall decide whether it is to be baptized or not.

*Ibid., § 26.*

694. If a Preacher learns that any of his parishioners has not, within the established six-week period, brought forward his infant to receive holy baptism, and when the reasons given by the parents, or the nearest relatives of the newborn, for further postponing the performance of this sacred rite are, in his opinion, not worthy of consideration, he shall first admonish them to conform to the existing provisions on this matter, and then, should these counsels and remarks prove ineffective, report the matter to the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 27.*

695. When it is reported to the Consistory by a parish Preacher that the parents, or nearest relatives, of a newborn infant, without reasons worthy of consideration and despite admonitions, fail to bring it forward for the reception of holy baptism even after the fixed six-week period, the Consistory notifies the chief local authority of this, which, after due investigation and examination of the matter, authorizes the Consistory to appoint an honest and God-fearing Christian as guardian of the infant solely for the purpose of performing holy baptism upon it.

*Ibid., § 28.*

696. Preachers perform holy baptism in a private home only when the poor health of the newborn or of its parents, cold or very bad weather, distance, or other reasons worthy of consideration prevent the infant from being brought to church. In all other respects, holy baptism performed in a private home follows the same order as in church, with prayer, and, if possible, with singing as well.

*Ibid., § 29.*

697. If, in the number or choice of names given to an infant at baptism, or in the designation of godparents, the Preacher finds anything openly unseemly or scandalous, he is obliged, by means of representations, admonitions, and proper explanations, to try to prevent the disorders and unpleasant consequences that might arise from this. Persons known for open godlessness, or for a depraved life disgracing the title of Christian, as well as those who present themselves for the baptism in a drunken state or improperly dressed, must not be admitted by the Preacher as godparents of the infant being baptized.

*Ibid., § 30.*

698. In all the Baltic governorates, illegitimate children of mothers of the Evangelical Protestant confession, as well as abandoned or foundling infants whose parents are unknown, may be baptized according to the rites of the Evangelical Lutheran Church, subject to observance of the general rules on this subject in the Statute on the Prevention and Suppression of Crimes. In the other regions of the Empire, Evangelical Lutheran Preachers are obliged to send infants brought to them for baptism whose parents are unknown, as appropriate, to the Orthodox clergy.

*Ibid., § 31.*

<...>

708. Preachers are to see to it that baptism out of necessity is performed only in the cases specified in article 160, and by no means out of laziness, or as a result of some superstitious custom or prejudice, or, finally, for the purpose of concealing something forbidden by law.

*Ibid., § 41.*

709. When women who have been delivered of a child appear in church after six weeks, the Preacher is obliged to perform the prayers designated for this occasion in the Church Agenda.

*Ibid., § 42.*

710. Firmness in faith and in the observance of Christian duties depends, among other things, greatly on the fullness and clarity of the knowledge of the Law of God acquired in early youth; for this reason, Preachers are charged with the sacred duty, with the constant zeal and precision demanded by their duty and conscience, to instruct in the dogmas and institutions of their Church all young men and women preparing for confirmation, devoting to this every year at least all the time absolutely necessary.

*Ibid., § 43.*

711. In addition to Luther's Small Catechism, Preachers may, in this instruction in the Law of God, use other textbooks as well, but only such as have been approved by the full assembly of the General Consistory upon the recommendation of the local Consistories concerning each book in particular.

*Ibid., § 44.*

712. Consistories may, in extraordinary cases, permit the performance of confirmation upon young men who have not yet reached the age of fifteen: observing, however, that this rite always be performed in accordance with the true purpose of its institution, that is, that the one being confirmed be sufficiently instructed in the Law of God and fully comprehend the importance and sanctity of the calling of a member of the Church. When a Preacher reports on those who present themselves for confirmation after reaching the age of eighteen, the Consistories examine what reasons prevented the candidate from fulfilling this duty within the time established for it, and if they note that it was missed through negligence or thoughtlessness, they issue, through the Preacher, an appropriate remark and admonition to him and to his parents or guardians, reporting this to the General Consistory and to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, which takes measures to prevent such occurrences.

*Ibid. § 45.*

713. Before performing the rite of confirmation, Preachers are obliged, in the presence of the parish, on a day appointed and announced well in advance for that purpose, to examine strictly those to be confirmed in the Law of God.

Note. If a Preacher is obliged to confirm a young man not instructed by himself in the Law of God, he must, before the general examination in the Church, satisfy himself as to the candidate's knowledge in a preliminary private examination.

*Ibid., § 46.*

714. Preachers are permitted, at their own discretion, to perform confirmation on the day appointed for the examination that must always precede it, or else on the following day, when those confirmed are admitted to Holy Communion; but to combine all three of these acts, especially when the number of those to be confirmed is very great, would be inconvenient and contrary to the purpose of this institution. A Preacher must not seek to render this solemnity — important and moving in itself — still more striking by resorting to any means not belonging to its essence in order to act upon the feelings.

*Ibid., § 47.*

715. Consistories are charged with the duty of establishing for their district, in accordance with local circumstances, precise and permanent rules as to how instruction before confirmation is to be given, addressing among other things the following points in particular: 1) Should young men attend instruction before confirmation together with young women, or separately? 2) How long is this instruction to continue; in this regard, a term of at least not less than six weeks should be set as a general rule, unless particular local circumstances require this period to be shortened? 3) How many hours per week, and at what time of day, must the Preacher give his instruction to the youth? 4) How many young men and young women may the Preacher instruct at one time, and how are the listeners to be divided when their number is very great?

*Ibid., § 48.*

716. The rite of general confession must be performed, when convenient, the day before Holy Communion, so that sufficient time remains afterward for each communicant's proper preparation; but where, owing to some local circumstances, this order cannot be observed, it is done on the very day of communion, though before the beginning of public worship.

*Ibid., § 49.*

717. If anyone feels the need to confess orally, in particular, to his spiritual father the sins that burden his conscience, or the doubts that trouble him, this is in no case to be forbidden him. Preachers are even obliged, when performing general confession, to explain to their listeners that such confession may be quite beneficial, presenting particular occasions for spiritual healing. Preachers are also obliged, with regard to those among those coming to them to make confession who, as is known to them, live in open enmity with one another (not, however, confusing with this litigation conducted without particular personal hatred), to incline them by their exhortations toward reconciliation; and if they answer that they are not yet ready for this, to advise them to refrain for a time from receiving the Holy Sacrament.

*Ibid., § 50.*

718. A Preacher is obliged to keep in inviolable secrecy everything entrusted to him in confession. Even at the demand of judicial authorities he may not disclose this without the consent of the person who confessed, but must endeavor by exhortation to induce him to voluntarily declare before the court the offense he has committed and the circumstances accompanying it.

*Ibid., § 51.*

719. If, however, the disclosure of what was said in confession is necessary to avert a danger threatening the Monarch, the Imperial House, or the state, then the Preacher is obliged, when he cannot persuade the penitent to make his own admission thereof, immediately to report this to the authorities, at first without naming the offender; but when the authorities, in order to avert the intended crime, deem it necessary to learn the name of the confessing party and demand this of the Preacher, he must name him, and in this case he is released from all responsibility for disclosing the secret of confession.

*Ibid., § 52.*

720. When a person whom rumor accuses of having committed some crime — one not, however, belonging to the state crimes designated above in Article 719, or who is already, or was previously, under trial for this — confesses before his spiritual father in confession to the commission of the crime of which he is suspected, or was suspected: the Preacher must endeavor, by means of exhortations, to incline him to declare this before the court; and if the offender, fearing punishment, does not resolve upon this, then to incline him at least to make restitution for the harm he has caused. If, in order to prevent a contemplated crime, or to stop the harmful consequences of a wrongdoing already committed, it is necessary to disclose it to the authorities, and the penitent will not agree himself to confess his offense before the court, or otherwise to avert the harm that would result from it: then he is refused absolution of sins and admission to Holy Communion, but what was said in confession is kept secret.

*Ibid., § 53.*

721. When a member of the Evangelical Lutheran Church belonging to some particular parish requests permission to make confession and receive Holy Communion not from his own parish Preacher, the Consistory is obliged first carefully to examine whether the reasons he presents for this truly deserve consideration.

*Ibid., § 54.*

722. A Preacher may not, of his own accord, exclude from public confession and reception of Holy Communion any member of the Evangelical Lutheran Church, except those deprived of reason or in a state of unconsciousness. If he is in doubt whether some hardened and notorious sinner, known to all, may be admitted to Holy Communion, he is obliged first of all, with Christian love, to explain his doubts on the matter to the person himself; and if, even after this, the person does not cease to demand admission to Holy Communion, the Preacher reports this case to the Consistory, without naming the sinner, but setting forth in detail the reasons for his doubt. Upon receiving such a report, the Consistory either permits him to admit the penitent to Holy Communion, or prescribes that he be excluded for a time from the Lord's Table; in the latter case it grants the Preacher the right to admit the sinner to Holy Communion as soon as he finds him worthy of it. The Consistory is to report every such temporary exclusion from Holy Communion, as well as any subsequent admission thereto, to the Ministry of Internal Affairs, with an exact description of the circumstances of the case, but likewise without indicating names.

*Ibid., § 55. DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 393*

723. Preachers are obliged carefully to admonish those of their parishioners who for a long time — for example, several years in a row — have not received Holy Communion, impressing upon them how necessary this communion with our Savior Jesus Christ is for every Christian; but on the other hand to advise all communicants, both in fulfilling this duty and afterward, to refrain carefully from everything by which the beneficial effect of this sacrament upon them might be weakened or entirely destroyed. Preachers strictly ensure that Holy Communion is not used to satisfy any superstitions.

*Ibid., § 56.*

724. If, during the celebration and administration of Holy Communion, the bread and wine consecrated upon the altar should prove insufficient, then the newly brought wine and bread must, before communion, likewise be consecrated, though without the pronouncement [of the full rite]. Likewise, the remaining holy elements must be carefully preserved and guarded against any unworthy use, or use tending toward the satisfaction of any superstitions.

*Ibid., § 57.*

725. A Preacher who, pursuant to the sentence of a judicial place, is charged by the Consistory with imposing church penance upon a person of the Evangelical Lutheran confession, must instruct both the sinner and the parish itself in the meaning and purpose of church penance, urge the former to sincere repentance, but at the same time also comfort him as the Holy Gospel teaches, and continue these exhortations and instructions until he is deemed worthy of reconciliation with the Church; as for the rest of the parishioners, he is obliged to remind them that no one has the right to reproach this person, now reconciled with the Church, for the church penance he has undergone or for his former offenses, but that everyone must see in him a brother in the faith restored to them.

*Ibid., § 58.*

726. When, instead of church penance, the court prescribes that the parish be informed of the sentence pronounced upon one of its members, the Preacher must make use of this sorrowful occasion to exhort and instruct his parishioners, endeavoring that they sincerely and unanimously pray to the Almighty that He may touch the sinner's heart and turn him to repentance.

*Ibid., § 59.*

727. If, at the marriage ceremony, the bridegroom or the bride, in answer to the question put to them by the Preacher, declares that he or she does not wish to enter into marriage with the other party present, the Preacher must immediately halt the performance of the marriage ceremony.

*Ibid., § 60.*

728. Preachers, depending on the circumstances and condition of the persons entering into marriage, may perform the marriage rite in private homes as well; but this is permitted only as an exception to the general rule.

Note. Marriages (Trauung) of the dangerously ill, if they are nevertheless in full possession of their faculties, are permitted when the sick person himself expressly demands it; but Preachers are obliged, through friendly counsel, to dissuade [people] from such marriages.

*Ibid., § 61.*

729. If the marriage rite is performed not by the Preacher who published the banns, or when the bridegroom and bride were announced in different churches, the Preacher who is to bless the marriage may not proceed with this until he has received, from those who conducted the publication of banns, proper certification that there are no impediments to the marriage.

*Ibid., § 62.*

730. Preachers are obliged to endeavor, by means of instruction and counsel, that their parishioners observe the established rules and proprieties with respect to the burial of the dead, avoiding, however, excessive pomp and needless expense.

*Ibid., § 63.*

731. In funeral orations, Preachers must carefully refrain both from excessive, inappropriate praise of the deceased and from an unseemly, severe judgment of their lives, keeping in view only the consolation of the relatives and friends of the person being buried, and the general spiritual edification of all who listen.

*Ibid., § 64.*

732. The performance of the burial rite in a church or in a private home must not be a cause for the cancellation, or even the delay, of the appointed public worship. During this worship on Sundays and holidays, it is not permitted to perform burials or to place bodies in the church.

*Ibid., § 65.*

733. Preachers are obliged, before proceeding to perform the burial rite, to ascertain precisely the day and hour of death of the person to be buried, and to see to it that no one is committed to the earth before the term established by law. They must, at every convenient occasion, remind their parishioners how dangerous it is to hasten burial, what are generally the reliable signs of death, and how one ought to proceed when doubt still exists. If they notice on the body of the deceased signs of violent death, or if rumors that have reached them and merit credence arouse in them suspicion on this account, then, without proceeding to perform the burial rite, they report this to the police authorities and await their instructions.

*Ibid., § 66.*

734. Consistories shall see to it that special buildings exist at cemeteries for placing bodies while awaiting burial (Leichenkammern). Where such buildings already exist, they are to be kept in order and intact; where they have not yet been established, the Consistories are obliged, through the Preachers subordinate to them, to induce parishioners to build them at common expense and labor. These buildings, however, should be simple and constructed at the smallest possible expense, especially in villages, where it is only necessary that they correspond to the purpose of their establishment, that is, that bodies may safely be left in them for two or three days. If the parishioners do not voluntarily agree to participate in the construction of these buildings, the Consistory reports this to the Ministry of Internal Affairs.

*Ibid., § 67. DOCUMENTS_________________________________________________________________________________ 395*

735. Consistories and all clergy are charged with the duty of strictly overseeing compliance with all police regulations concerning burial and the arrangement and maintenance of cemeteries.

*Ibid., § 68.*

III. On marriages.

736. Preachers are obliged, with due seriousness, to admonish persons wishing to become betrothed or to have their banns published, that they should prepare to enter the sacred union of marriage as befits Christians, with prayers for the mercy, help, and blessing of the Almighty, and with a quiet, modest way of life, and that until the marriage rite is performed they should refrain from any relations between themselves not permitted before that time.

1832 Dec. 28 (5871) § 69.

737. Preachers must draw the attention of persons wishing to become betrothed to the conditions necessary for marriage and the lawful impediments thereto, and before the publication of banns and the performance of the marriage rite must, as far as possible, satisfy themselves that there are no impediments to the impending marriage.

*Ibid., § 70.*

738. If the Preacher has any doubt on this matter, he must have recourse to the counsel of his Probst or Superintendent, and in more important cases seek also the authorization of the Consistory.

*Ibid., § 71.*

739. Preachers may publish the banns of widowers and widows, or of divorced spouses, entering into a new marriage, only after obtaining from them lawful certification from the proper Guardianship and Orphans' Court offices that, in the opinion [of those bodies], there is, with regard to the children of their former marriage, no impediment to their entering into a new one. Where local circumstances make it difficult to furnish such a certificate, it is sufficient if the person wishing to enter into a new marriage and two witnesses, assuming responsibility for all consequences, declare under oath that the other party left no property behind; the Preacher must only see to it that not just anyone indiscriminately, but so far as possible always reliable persons, are admitted as witnesses.

*Ibid., § 72.*

740. Preachers must not publish the banns of divorced spouses who have not been deprived of the right, or who have obtained permission, to enter into a new marriage, until they have produced the proper divorce decree and a certificate from the Consistory that lawful execution has already been made pursuant to that decree.

*Ibid., § 73.*

741. Preachers are obliged, with every possible effort, to dissuade from entering into marriage the decrepit, those afflicted with incurable diseases, or those suffering from serious bodily defects, the feeble-minded, and in general all who are incapable of marriage and household management. If, however, they are absolutely determined to enter into marriage, the Preacher is obliged, before the publication of banns, to report this, setting forth all the circumstances, to the Consistory, which communicates with the appropriate official body and, upon receiving its response, conveys it to the Preacher. However, entry into marriage may be forbidden only when, upon due investigation and on the testimony of a physician, they are declared incapable of it, and when it is moreover proven that they are in no way able to support themselves along with a family.

*Ibid., § 74.*

742. The publication of banns must always be read from the pulpit by the Preacher himself, in the parish church, at the conclusion of the sermon; it must be followed by a brief prayer for those whose banns are announced. If, in the parish of the bridegroom or bride, worship is not conducted by the Preacher himself every Sunday, and is generally infrequent, the publication of banns may be performed by the sexton, or by a reader, in the order prescribed by the Preacher.

*Ibid., § 75.*

743. Although the Preacher is permitted (Arts. 230, 231), in extraordinary cases, to limit himself to a twofold, or even a single, publication of banns, this is allowed only if all the personal circumstances of the bridegroom and bride are sufficiently known to him, or reliably attested. He is charged with the duty of acting in such cases with the utmost caution, and of reporting them without delay to the Consistory, stating also the reasons that induced him to depart from the ordinary rules. When the publication of banns is limited to a single occasion, the Preacher's report on this must be accompanied, in the original or in a certified copy, by the order of the authorities pursuant to which the betrothed person is being sent on a journey or campaign, or else by a physician's certificate of his serious illness.

*Ibid., § 76.*

744. If a person unknown [to the Preacher] wishes to become betrothed or to have banns published, the Preacher is obliged first to require of that person sufficient proof, or a certificate issued, under their own responsibility, by at least two trustworthy persons, both as to the origin of that person and as to whether she is entitled to enter into the proposed marriage, and whether she belongs to the Evangelical Protestant Church. If the person requesting betrothal or the publication of banns cannot produce such proof or certificate, then notice of her intention to marry must be published three times in the gazettes, with a period of six months fixed for the declaration of objection, and with an indication of the name and place of residence of the Preacher to whom she applied with the request for publication of banns or betrothal. This publication is made by the Consistory. If, upon the expiration of the six-month period, no objection has been declared by anyone, the Preacher proceeds to the betrothal, or the publication of banns for the marriage, but only after requiring from the person unknown to him who wishes to enter into marriage a written declaration that there are no lawful impediments to this.

*Ibid., § 77.*

745. If, during the publication of banns, or during the very performance of the marriage rite, the Preacher receives notice — even from an outside party having no right (Arts. 247, 248) to oppose the marriage — that there is an impediment to its performance, he is obliged to suspend the further performance of the rite and immediately demand proof from the person who declared this impediment. When DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 397

proof worthy of consideration is presented, he postpones the marriage until the doubt that has arisen is resolved.

*Ibid., § 78.*

IV. On the examination of candidates for the clergy.

746. The Evangelical Lutheran Consistories must not admit to examination those candidates who may, with sufficient grounds, be accused of thoughtlessness, of negligence in the performance of their duties, and especially of a life contrary to the rules of morality. The Consistory has the right to investigate beforehand what the conduct of the candidate so accused has been, and if it finds these accusations well-founded, it refuses to admit him to examination until he presents proof, worthy of consideration, of his reform.

1832 Dec. 28 (5871) § 79.

747. When a person wishing to obtain the right to preach (veniam concionandi) has submitted, in accordance with Article 271, the required certificates and a brief account of the events of his life (curriculum vitae), the Consistory assigns him several topics for written compositions, in order to see whether he is capable of treating any subject clearly and thoroughly and whether he has acquired sufficient skill in thinking it through and in using book resources with discernment. These topics must relate: 1) to exegetical-dogmatic subjects, in Latin; 2) to subjects of Church History, or Christian Moral Doctrine, or both, in German or another modern language; 3) specifically to preaching, with the assignment of Biblical texts for sermons and a detailed indication of the order of exposition in the language in which he wishes to obtain the right to preach.

*Ibid., § 80.*

748. These compositions must be submitted within a year, unless prevented by a serious and prolonged illness; otherwise the candidate is given new assignments. The submitted compositions are carefully examined by the examiners, and each of them states his opinion of them in writing. If they prove unsatisfactory in content or in manner of exposition, the candidate is not admitted to the oral examination, but is obliged to correct the compositions he has submitted, or else receives new topics. If the compositions are found satisfactory, the candidate is admitted to the oral examination, and a text is assigned to him for the sermon belonging to this examination.

*Ibid., § 81.*

749. The examination for obtaining the right to preach (pro venia concionandi) is divided into four parts:

1) The General Superintendent, Superintendent, or another clergyman appointed by the Consistory to conduct the examination, assigns the candidate subjects for brief theological compositions, both in Latin and in the language in which he wishes to preach, and, in addition, a text from the Bible for the composition of an extended discourse, or sermon, upon it. These compositions must be written in the presence of the person conducting the examination, at the appointed time, and without any preparation (ex tempore), so that it may thereby be verified that the candidate himself, and without any outside assistance, composed also the compositions he previously submitted, and so that his ability to set forth his thoughts on spiritual subjects quickly and clearly may be ascertained.

2) In order to ascertain precisely whether the examinee has the proper general education (humanistische Bildung), the person conducting the examination assigns him passages from ancient classical authors in Greek and Latin, for translation and interpretation.

3) The candidate must, in the presence of at least one of the examiners, deliver a sermon on a text assigned to him, in order thereby to give a precise idea not only of his knowledge of Homiletics, but also of his memory, of the greater or lesser pleasantness of his voice and delivery, and in general of his ability and skill in speaking from the pulpit.

4) Finally, the candidate is subjected to an oral examination in the Exegesis of the Old and New Testaments, in Dogmatics, Symbolics, Moral Doctrine, the History of the Church and of Dogmas, Philosophy, and Homiletics. In exegetical, historical, and dogmatic theology the examination is conducted in Latin; in the other parts, in German or another modern language.

*Ibid., § 82.*

750. No more than three candidates are ever to be summoned to examination at one time.

*Ibid., § 83.*

751. Examinations are conducted by the clerical members of the Consistory in the official chamber. Lay members may be present at these examinations.

*Ibid. § 84.*

752. The Consistory's determinations, both regarding the candidate's written compositions and his oral examination, are entered into a protocol drawn up according to the form attached hereto, which is signed by all the examiners. This protocol must always indicate specifically:

1) Whether the examinee is able to express his thoughts correctly, in a manner clear to everyone, and with due force and gravity, both orally and in writing, in German, or in the languages in which he wishes to preach?

2) Whether he can speak and write correctly and fluently in Latin?

3) Whether he is able to translate and grammatically analyze any passage of the Old Testament in Hebrew (Grund-Text)?

4) Whether he can translate the New Testament from the Greek (Grund-Text) and explain it?

5) Whether he has a clear and complete understanding of the doctrine of faith and morals of the Gospel, and whether he is thoroughly acquainted with the Symbolic books of the Evangelical Lutheran Church?

6) Whether he can, without difficulty, indicate the most notable epochs of Church History and of Dogmas, point out the causes and consequences of the most important events, and give a satisfactory account of the History of the principal schisms and sects?

7) Whether he has thorough knowledge of Logic, Psychology, and the History of Philosophy?

8) Whether he is acquainted with the necessary conditions for an edifying sermon, and whether he can, in proper order, clearly and precisely interpret any Biblical text?

9) Whether he has the necessary external abilities for delivering sermons, and whether he delivered the sermon belonging to his examination without notes (concept)?

*Ibid., § 85.*

753. If the examinee has satisfied all the above requirements (Art. 752) and has, in some parts, displayed excellent abilities and knowledge, and it is moreover evident that he is animated by true Evangelical teaching, then he receives the right to preach (veniam concionandi), and it is indicated in the certificate that he displayed excellent abilities and knowledge.

If the candidate has earned, in all parts, at least the approval of the examiners, he receives the same right, and it is indicated in the certificate that he has good abilities and knowledge.

Whoever, in some one subject, could not obtain full approval, but in general displayed sufficient knowledge, and moreover was noted to show a striving toward further improvement, receives the right to preach, and it is indicated in the certificate that he has sufficient abilities and knowledge.

*Ibid., § 86.*

754. A candidate is refused permission to preach if the Consistory notes in him either complete ignorance of the original text of the Old Testament, or insufficient knowledge of the original text of the New Testament, or an inability to express his thoughts correctly and clearly in German or in the language in which the candidate wishes to preach, or ignorance of the Latin language, or weak knowledge of the doctrine of faith and morals of the Evangelical Lutheran Church, or finally deficiencies in the very manner of preaching that might produce a poor impression upon listeners. Any one of the above-mentioned deficiencies is sufficient grounds for refusal.

*Ibid., § 87.*

755. If the candidate's incapacity arises more from imperfect education than from natural deficiencies, he may, after fresh preparation, present himself for a second examination upon the expiration of a year.

*Ibid., § 88.*

756. The protocol and the certificate must indicate in which languages, besides German, the candidate has been granted permission to preach. If a candidate subsequently attains such proficiency in any of the local vernacular languages that he is capable of preaching in it, he may present the proper proof of this to the Consistory, and if it deems it sufficient, he receives from it the right to do so.

*Ibid., § 89.*

757. If a candidate wishing to undergo examination for obtaining the rank of Preacher submits the certificates specified in Article 277, he is first given certain assignments for written compositions, of which, apart from the sermon text, at least one must be drawn from Practical Theology. From these assignments, with the exception, however, of the sermon, the Consistory may in some cases exempt those who were rated excellent in the examination for obtaining the right to preach.

*Ibid. § 90.*

758. In examining the compositions submitted at this examination, the same rules established above, in Article 749, are observed.

*Ibid., § 91.*

759. In this examination the rules set forth above, in Article 752, are likewise observed, with the sole exception of the examination in ancient languages. Instead, the candidate must demonstrate a trial lesson teaching certain passages, chosen by himself, from the Catechism in the language of the parish to which he wishes to be appointed.

*Ibid., § 92.*

760. The oral examination at the second examination (pro ministerio) differs from that to which the candidate is subjected at the first (pro venia concionandi) not so much in the subjects comprising it as in the fact that at this stage more extensive knowledge, complete thoroughness and clarity of concepts, and greater maturity of judgment are required. The examination must not be limited to Homiletics alone, but extends to all parts of Practical Theology and to knowledge of the Church Statute. Since Preachers exert an important influence on the education of youth, and the school must be regarded as the antechamber of the Church, it is necessary that the candidate also be examined in his knowledge of Pedagogy, and especially in the Methodology of elementary instruction.

*Ibid., § 93.*

761. The examination protocol is drawn up according to the form attached hereto. Particular attention is given to whether the candidate made use of the instructions and remarks given to him at the first examination, whether he has acquired new knowledge, especially in Holy Scripture and the teaching of the Evangelical Lutheran Church, whether he already possesses all the means necessary for preaching the Gospel — in a word, whether he is capable of discharging the pastoral office, and to which of the three above-mentioned ratings — excellent, good, or sufficient — he is found worthy.

*Ibid., § 94.*

762. At the second examination (pro ministerio) a candidate is refused the right to occupy a Preacher's position if:

1) During the examination, or during catechization, or in a sermon delivered by him, he permitted himself thoughtless judgments regarding the truths of Christianity or church institutions; or

2) He cannot correctly, definitely, clearly, and comprehensibly express his thoughts in German or in the language in which he is to preach; or

3) He cannot write a Latin composition without significant errors; or

4) Since the time of the first examination (pro venia concionandi) he has shown no progress whatsoever in knowledge of the original text of the Old and New Testaments and has not grasped its essence and spirit; or DOCUMENTS____________________________________________________________________________ 401

5) He does not fully grasp the fundamental rules of faith and morality, so that he is unable to interpret them clearly and cannot defend their principal tenets; or

6) He is unable to state precisely at least the most important events of Church History and the origin of Symbolic Theology; or

7) He does not have thorough knowledge of the provisions of the Church Statute; or

8) In catechization and preaching he displayed an evident deficiency, not only in skill, which is acquired and perfected through experience, but also in judgment itself and in the knowledge needed to explain the sacred truths of Christianity; or finally

9) Being unable to know the sermon by heart, is always compelled to read it, or has too unpleasant a voice, and moreover poor, indistinct pronunciation, and in general such an appearance or habits as give cause to fear that his preaching will produce upon the listeners an unfavorable effect incompatible with its purpose.

*Ibid., § 95.*

763. The determination of whether a candidate is capable of occupying the position of Preacher is indicated, together with the attestation he has received, in the last column of the protocol, which is signed by the examiners. In accordance with this determination the candidate is issued a certificate with the appropriate attestation, or he is refused one.

*Ibid., § 96.*

764. A candidate who has not been granted an approving certificate (pro ministerio) is permitted to appear again for examination, but not before a year has elapsed.

*Ibid., § 97.*

765. The examination for the right to obtain the position of Preacher is conducted by the clerical members of the Consistory, in the meeting room, with open doors; lay members may be present at this examination.

*Ibid., § 98.*

766. In order that no one who has received a refusal at the first or second examination (pro venia concionandi, vel pro ministerio) may present himself with a request for examination in another Consistory before the appointed term, the names of these candidates are communicated each time to all Consistories in the state.

*Ibid., § 99.*

767. If a candidate who was found incapable at any of the aforementioned examinations by one Consistory is subsequently examined in another and receives an approving certificate from it, the first Consistory is nevertheless not obligated to appoint him Preacher within its district without first satisfying itself of his abilities by means of a theological conversation.

Note. Upon completion of the examination (pro venia concionandi) candidates of the clergy enter for one year as Assistants to Pastors chosen by the Consistory, in order that the cast of mind and morals of these candidates may be ascertained (art. 281).

*Ibid., § 100; 1851 Dec. 24 (25845); 1856 Oct. 23 (31044).*

V. On the Duties of Church Wardens and Elders.

768. Church Boards of Trustees are obliged, by all means within their power, to assist their parish Preacher in his labors aimed at the spiritual welfare of the parishioners, removing as far as possible everything that might hinder the success of his useful efforts. They must in particular strive to ease for him the oversight of the education of youth and in general the establishment of true piety and good morals in the parish, and likewise to provide him with the means for the unimpeded and fitting performance of divine services, the observance of Sundays and other holy days, and the visiting and care of the sick and poor found within the parish.

1832 Dec. 28 (5871) § 101.

769. Church Boards of Trustees are also obliged to observe good order in the church and in general order during divine services, assisting the Preacher in this at his request and at their own discretion.

*Ibid. § 102.*

770. When the Preacher, owing to illness, is unable to perform his duties, the Church Board of Trustees immediately notifies the Provost, or, where there are no Provosts, the Superintendent, or the General Superintendent.

*Ibid., § 103.*

771. When a vacancy arises owing to the death or complete incapacity of the Preacher, the Trustees must strive to see that proper measures are taken for entrusting the temporary performance of his duties, and then for the speediest appointment of another Preacher to his place; they are present at the election of the Preacher and at his induction into office.

*Ibid., § 104.*

772. In parishes located at a great distance from the Provost and Consistory, the very induction of new Preachers into office is entrusted to the Church Trustees by order of the Consistory.

*Ibid. § 105.*

773. Upon the induction of the Preacher into office, they hand over to him the church books, parish registers, and such church property as ought to be in his keeping, together with the appropriate inventories and account books thereof.

*Ibid. § 106.*

774. Church Boards of Trustees see to it that cemeteries are laid out in accordance with the regulations existing for this purpose, and, as far as possible, that special buildings for the laying-out of bodies before burial (Leichen-Kammern) are established everywhere.

*Ibid., § 107.*

775. Church Trustees, together with the Preacher, exercise direct supervision over the Church Elders drawn from among the peasants.

*Ibid., § 108.*

776. Church Elders drawn from among the peasants must observe the conduct and manner of life of parishioners of the lower estates, especially the upbringing of children and their instruction at home; they are also obliged, paying attention to bad customs and vices appearing among the

peasants, to admonish those who indulge in them and to report this to the Preacher.

*Ibid., § 109.*

777. Church Elders also observe the conduct of teachers at rural schools.

*Ibid., § 110.*

778. Church Elders notify the Preacher, or the Church Trustees, depending on the nature of the matter, of all unusual occurrences of a church-related nature.

*Ibid., §111.*

779. For attendance at divine services, Church Elders are obliged to present themselves to the Preacher in good time; when they cannot do so, they send in their place other peasants of good conduct.

*Ibid., § 112.*

780. Gathering by duty at church on Sundays and holy days, they inform the Preacher of all sick persons in the parish; in the case of dangerous epidemic diseases, they report this to him immediately and before the Sunday or holy day, notifying him in good time whether the sick wish to avail themselves of his spiritual instruction.

*Ibid., § 113.*

781. They see to it that domestic servants and other parishioners of the lower estates are not, without important cause, drawn away from the duty of attending divine services, and, when necessary, bring their observations on this matter to the attention of the Preacher and the Church Trustees.

*Ibid., § 114.*

782. In case of disorder during divine services, the Church Elders, at the Preacher's request, assist him in taking the necessary measures to stop such disorder.

*Ibid., § 115.*

783. Church Elders receive at their churches voluntary offerings made in their favor.

*Ibid., § 116.*

784. Church Elders must be present at the induction of the Preacher into office.

*Ibid., § 117.*

785. They must also be present at all church visitations carried out in the parish.

*Ibid., § 118.*

786. When parishioners are convened to deliberate on church affairs, Church Elders are especially obliged to attend these parish assemblies.

*Ibid., § 119.*

787. At burials they are entrusted with the oversight of proper order in the lowering of coffins into the grave.

*Ibid., § 120.*

788. Church Elders see to the proper delivery of materials for church construction and to it that the number of workers required, according to the instructions given or the agreement made, is provided.

*Ibid., § 121.*

789. In extraordinary cases, when it is not possible to send a necessary instruction or report concerning church administration by post, the Church Elders are obliged to take measures for delivering it to its proper destination.

*Ibid., § 122.*

#### SECTION TWO. SPECIAL PROVISIONS ON THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE SPIRITUAL AFFAIRS OF CERTAIN SOCIETIES OF THE PROTESTANT CONFESSION.

##### CHAPTER ONE.

On the Administration of the Spiritual Affairs

of Evangelical Reformed Societies.

Division One.

General Provisions.

790. The district administration of Evangelical Reformed spiritual affairs in the Western governorates belongs to the Synod and Collegium of this confession, established in Vilna; in the other governorates it belongs to the local Evangelical Lutheran Consistories, whose sessions, held for the discussion and decision of matters proper to this confession, are altered according to the rules set out below in their composition and are named Reformed Sessions.

See the enactments cited under articles 791—796.

791. The Vilna Evangelical Reformed Synod has no fixed number of members; it is composed of all honored persons of the Reformed confession of clerical and noble rank of the Western territory of the Empire, and assembles once or twice a year to decide the most important matters concerning the Evangelical Reformed churches under its jurisdiction; the management of current affairs, however, it entrusts to the Vilna Evangelical Reformed Collegium.

1768 Feb. 13 (13071) art. 2, § 5; 1830 Jul. 15 (3796); 1840 Oct. 11 (13854).

792. The presence of the Vilna Evangelical Reformed Collegium is composed of a President from among lay persons, a Vice-President from among clergy, three members likewise from among clergy, and three members from among lay persons. Attached to it is a Chancery, consisting of a Secretary General, a Recorder, a Registrar, and a fixed number of chancery servants.

1831 Jun. 24 (4674).

793. The President and Vice-President of the Collegium (art. 792) are elected by the Synod and confirmed by the Minister of Internal Affairs. The appointment of all its other officers depends on the Synod itself.

*Ibid.*

794. The lay members of the Collegium and the officers of its Chancery (art. 792) are considered to be in state service.

*Ibid.*

795. In each local Evangelical Lutheran Consistory, when spiritual matters of Evangelical Reformed societies are examined and decided therein, there are present, in place of clerical members of the Evangelical Lutheran confession, one, and where possible two, of the Pastors and an equal number of Church Elders of the Evangelical Reformed confession.

1830 Jul. 15 (3796); 1832 Feb. 2 (5126); 1834 Apr. 17 (6999); 1837 Mar. 31 (10086).

796. The election and confirmation of Pastors of the Evangelical Reformed confession, the examinations and ordination of candidates to holy orders, and the procedure for appointing to these Pastorates foreigners who wish it, already examined and ordained, are carried out according to the Laws on the Estates, articles 372—375.

*Ibid.; 1840 Oct. 11 (13854); 1842 May 19 (15658).*

797. In case of complaints against a Pastor or Elder of the Evangelical Reformed confession sitting in an Evangelical Lutheran Consistory, the Ministry of Internal Affairs, upon report thereof by the Consistory, appoints, for the investigation of the complaints, a deputy chosen from persons of the Evangelical Reformed confession belonging to the rank of the accused. In the further conduct of matters of this kind the judicial procedure set forth above in the Statute of the Evangelical Lutheran Church is observed, except in matters concerning the dogmas of the faith, which are in every case submitted for the Highest consideration.

See the enactments cited under article 795.

Division Two.

Special Provisions.

I. On the Administration of the Spiritual Affairs

of the St. Petersburg Evangelical Reformed Society.
